source_arguments.name: RHTower.thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing_mean_bracket
source_arguments.statement:
theorem thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing_mean_bracket
    {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hBnx : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (-x)) :
    thetaCuspLikelihoodMean (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate x) <
        thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing x ∧
      thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing x <
        thetaCuspLikelihoodMean (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (-x))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing_mean_bracket
    {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hBnx : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (-x)) :
    thetaCuspLikelihoodMean (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate x) <
        thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing x ∧
      thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing x <
        thetaCuspLikelihoodMean (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (-x))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let a := thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (-x)
  let b := thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate x
  let f := fun B : ℝ => Real.log (thetaCuspLikelihoodPartition B)
  let f' := fun B : ℝ => -thetaCuspLikelihoodMean B
  have hab : a < b := thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate_neg_lt hx
  have ha : 0 < a := hBnx
  have hb : 0 < b := ha.trans hab
  have hcont : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b) := by
    intro B hB
    exact (hasDerivAt_log_thetaCuspLikelihoodPartition_cumulant
      (ha.trans_le hB.1)).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
  have hderiv : ∀ B ∈ Set.Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' B) B := by
    intro B hB
    exact hasDerivAt_log_thetaCuspLikelihoodPartition_cumulant
      (ha.trans hB.1)
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hslope⟩ :=
    exists_hasDerivAt_eq_slope f f' hab hcont hderiv
  have hcross : thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing x =
      thetaCuspLikelihoodMean c := by
    rw [thetaCuspLikelihoodSeamCrossing_eq_logPartition_secant hx hBnx]
    change (f a - f b) / (b - a) = thetaCuspLikelihoodMean c
    have hden : b - a ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hab.ne'
    have hslope' := (eq_div_iff hden).mp hslope
    apply (div_eq_iff hden).mpr
    dsimp [f, f'] at hslope' ⊢
    linarith
  rw [hcross]
  constructor
  · exact strictAntiOn_thetaCuspLikelihoodMean (ha.trans hc.1) hb hc.2
  · exact strictAntiOn_thetaCuspLikelihoodMean ha (ha.trans hc.1) hc.1

theorem abs_heatGauss_sub_zero_le {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1)

    (n : ℤ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :

    (n : ℤ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :

        heatTailDerivativeMajorant n)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let C : ℝ := (3 / (2 * x)) * Real.exp (-(Real.pi / (4 * x))) *
    heatTailDerivativeMajorant n
  have hdiff : ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) theta, DifferentiableAt ℝ (heatGauss x n) t := by
    intro t ht
    exact (hasDerivAt_heatGauss_phase x n t).differentiableAt
  have hbound : ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) theta,
      ‖fderiv ℝ (heatGauss x n) t‖ ≤ C := by
    intro t ht
    have hderiv := hasDerivAt_heatGauss_phase x n t
    rw [hderiv.hasFDerivAt.fderiv, ContinuousLinearMap.norm_toSpanSingleton,
      Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, abs_neg, abs_div,
      abs_of_pos (mul_pos (mul_pos (by positivity) Real.pi_pos) hx),
      abs_of_pos (heatGauss_pos x n t)]
    have htpi : t ≤ Real.pi := ht.2.trans htheta1
    have hgauss := heatGauss_le_majorant_closed hx hx1 ht.1 htpi n hn
    have hdist : |t - 2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ)| ≤
        3 * Real.pi * |(n : ℝ)| := by
      have hnabs : (1 : ℝ) ≤ |(n : ℝ)| := by
        have : (1 : ℤ) ≤ |n| := Int.one_le_abs (by exact_mod_cast hn)
        calc
          (1 : ℝ) = ((1 : ℤ) : ℝ) := by norm_num
          _ ≤ ((|n| : ℤ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast this
          _ = |(n : ℝ)| := by push_cast [Int.cast_abs]; ring
      calc
        |t - 2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ)|
            ≤ |t| + |2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ)| := abs_sub _ _
        _ = t + 2 * Real.pi * |(n : ℝ)| := by
          rw [abs_of_nonneg ht.1, abs_mul,
            abs_of_pos (by positivity : 0 < 2 * Real.pi)]
        _ ≤ 3 * Real.pi * |(n : ℝ)| := by
          nlinarith [htpi, Real.pi_pos]
    dsimp [C, heatTailDerivativeMajorant]
    have hden : 0 < 2 * Real.pi * x := by positivity
    calc
      |t - 2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ)| / (2 * Real.pi * x) * heatGauss x n t
          ≤ (3 * Real.pi * |(n : ℝ)|) / (2 * Real.pi * x) *
            (Real.exp (-(Real.pi / (4 * x))) * heatTailMajorant n) := by
              gcongr
              exact (heatGauss_pos x n t).le
      _ = (3 / (2 * x)) * Real.exp (-(Real.pi / (4 * x))) *
            (|(n : ℝ)| * heatTailMajorant n) := by
              field_simp
  have hmv := (convex_Icc (0 : ℝ) theta).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le
    hdiff hbound ⟨le_rfl, htheta0⟩ ⟨htheta0, le_rfl⟩

theorem norm_dyadicSharpPrimeWindow_cellError_le
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) {s : ℂ} (hsre : 0 < s.re)
    (j : ℕ) :
    ‖(((k + j : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s)) -
        ∫ x in ((k + j : ℕ) : ℝ)..(((k + j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1),
          (x : ℂ) ^ (-s)‖ ≤
      ‖s‖ * (k : ℝ) ^ (-s.re - 1)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem norm_dyadicSharpPrimeWindow_cellError_le
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) {s : ℂ} (hsre : 0 < s.re)
    (j : ℕ) :
    ‖(((k + j : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s)) -
        ∫ x in ((k + j : ℕ) : ℝ)..(((k + j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1),
          (x : ℂ) ^ (-s)‖ ≤
      ‖s‖ * (k : ℝ) ^ (-s.re - 1)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by
    intro hs
    rw [hs, Complex.zero_re] at hsre
    exact (lt_irrefl 0 hsre).elim
  let a : ℝ := (k + j : ℕ)
  let f : ℝ → ℂ := fun x => (x : ℂ) ^ (-s)
  let C : ℝ := ‖s‖ * (k : ℝ) ^ (-s.re - 1)
  have hkpos : (0 : ℝ) < k := by exact_mod_cast (show 0 < k by omega)
  have hapos : 0 < a := by
    dsimp only [a]
    exact_mod_cast (show 0 < k + j by omega)
  have hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a (a + 1),
      HasDerivWithinAt f ((-s) * (x : ℂ) ^ (-s - 1)) (Set.Icc a (a + 1)) x := by
    intro x hx
    have hxpos : 0 < x := lt_of_lt_of_le hapos hx.1
    exact (hasDerivAt_ofReal_cpow_const (ne_of_gt hxpos)
      (neg_ne_zero.mpr hs0)).hasDerivWithinAt
  have hderivBound : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ico a (a + 1),
      ‖(-s) * (x : ℂ) ^ (-s - 1)‖ ≤ C := by
    intro x hx
    have hxpos : 0 < x := lt_of_lt_of_le hapos hx.1
    have hkx : (k : ℝ) ≤ x := by
      have hka : (k : ℝ) ≤ a := by
        dsimp only [a]
        exact_mod_cast (show k ≤ k + j by omega)
      exact hka.trans hx.1
    have hexp : 0 ≤ s.re + 1 := by linarith
    have hpows : (k : ℝ) ^ (s.re + 1) ≤ x ^ (s.re + 1) :=
      Real.rpow_le_rpow hkpos.le hkx hexp
    have hkpowpos : 0 < (k : ℝ) ^ (s.re + 1) :=
      Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hkpos _
    have hrpow : x ^ (-s.re - 1) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ (-s.re - 1) := by
      rw [show -s.re - 1 = -(s.re + 1) by ring,
        Real.rpow_neg hxpos.le, Real.rpow_neg hkpos.le]
      simpa only [one_div] using one_div_le_one_div_of_le hkpowpos hpows
    rw [norm_mul, norm_neg, Complex.norm_cpow_eq_rpow_re_of_pos hxpos]
    simp only [Complex.sub_re, Complex.neg_re, Complex.one_re]
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hrpow (norm_nonneg s)
  have hmv : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a (a + 1), ‖f x - f a‖ ≤ C * (x - a) :=
    fun x hx => norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment' hderiv hderivBound x hx
  have hC : 0 ≤ C := mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg s) (Real.rpow_nonneg hkpos.le _)
  have hpoint : ∀ x ∈ Set.uIoc a (a + 1), ‖f a - f x‖ ≤ C := by
    intro x hx
    rw [Set.uIoc_of_le (by linarith)] at hx
    have hxa : x - a ≤ 1 := by linarith [hx.2]
    calc
      ‖f a - f x‖ = ‖f x - f a‖ := by rw [norm_sub_rev]
      _ ≤ C * (x - a) := hmv x ⟨hx.1.le, hx.2⟩
      _ ≤ C := by nlinarith
  have hfint := intervalIntegrable_ofReal_cpow_neg_on_natCell (j := j) hk s
  have hconst : IntervalIntegrable (fun _ : ℝ => f a) volume a (a + 1) :=
    intervalIntegrable_const
  calc
    ‖(((k + j : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s)) -
        ∫ x in ((k + j : ℕ) : ℝ)..(((k + j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1),
          (x : ℂ) ^ (-s)‖ =
      ‖∫ x in a..(a + 1), f a - f x‖ := by
        change ‖f a - ∫ x in a..(a + 1), f x‖ = _
        rw [intervalIntegral.integral_sub hconst hfint,
          intervalIntegral.integral_const]
        have haone : a + 1 - a = 1 := by ring
        rw [haone, one_smul]
    _ ≤ C * |a + 1 - a| := intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const hpoint
    _ = ‖s‖ * (k : ℝ) ^ (-s.re - 1) := by
      have haone : a + 1 - a = 1 := by ring
      rw [haone, abs_one, mul_one]

by
  have hderiv := tendsto_logWeibullExponent_deriv_zero hγ
  rw [Metric.tendsto_atTop]
  intro ε hε
  let C := ε / (r + 1)
  have hC : 0 < C := div_pos hε (by linarith)
  have hderivNorm : Tendsto
      (fun x : ℝ => ‖γ * (Real.log x) ^ (γ - 1) / x‖) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa using hderiv.norm
  have hsmall := hderivNorm.eventually_lt_const hC
  obtain ⟨Y, hY⟩ := Filter.eventually_atTop.mp hsmall
  refine ⟨max Y 2, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  have hxY : Y ≤ x := (le_max_left Y 2).trans hx
  have hx2 : 2 ≤ x := (le_max_right Y 2).trans hx
  have hxr : x ≤ x + r := by linarith
  have hdiff : ‖logWeibullExponent γ (x + r) - logWeibullExponent γ x‖ ≤
      C * ‖(x + r) - x‖ := by
    apply (convex_Icc x (x + r)).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le
      (f := logWeibullExponent γ)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hasDerivAt_logWeibullExponent γ (by linarith [hy.1])).differentiableAt
    · intro y hy
      rw [(hasDerivAt_logWeibullExponent γ (by linarith [hy.1])).deriv]
      exact (hY y (hxY.trans hy.1)).le
    · exact left_mem_Icc.mpr hxr
    · exact right_mem_Icc.mpr hxr
  have hrnorm : ‖(x + r) - x‖ = r := by
    rw [show x + r - x = r by ring, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hr]
  rw [hrnorm] at hdiff
  have hCr : C * r < ε := by
    dsimp [C]
    rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div]
    exact (div_lt_iff₀ (by linarith : 0 < r + 1)).2 (by nlinarith)
  simpa only [dist_zero_right] using hdiff.trans_lt hCr

## Cycle 142 — **THEOREM 49: smoothing cannot close the pointwise/mean-value gap**

Theorem 48 named the obstruction: every structural feature is optimal, every tool is a mean-value
tool. Cycle 142 attacks the standard bridge from mean-value to pointwise — the Sobolev inequality —
which the campaign already carries in `HTGeometry/SpikeSobolev.lean`.

### C368 — the two terms are not symmetric `[PROVED, LEAN-CERTIFIED]`

    |f(t₀)|²  ≤  (1/H)∫_I |f|²  +  ∫_I |f||f'| .

**Only the first term carries `1/H`.** For the frontier sum `F(t) = Σ_{n∼N}n^{−it}` one has
`F'(t) = −i Σ_n (\log n)n^{−it}`, so `∫_I|F'|² ≍ \log²N·∫_I|F|²` and

    ∫_I |F||F'| ≤ (∫_I|F|²)^{1/2}(∫_I|F'|²)^{1/2} ≍ **\log N · ∫_I |F|²** .

The variation term is *larger than the mean square itself*, with no `H` to shrink it.

### C369 — and the mean square is not `HN` on short intervals `[PROVED, LEAN-CERTIFIED]`

`∫_I|F|² = H·N + O(Σ_{m≠n}\min(H, N/|m−n|)) = H·N + O(N²\log N)`, so the off-diagonal dominates for
every `H ≪ N`. In exponents (`shortMeanSquare`), the mean square saturates at `N²` for all `H ≤ N`
(`shortMeanSquare_short`).

> **`[THEOREM 49]` The Sobolev upgrade returns the trivial bound at every interval length:
> `sobolevOutput h = 2` for all `h ≤ 1`, i.e. `|F| ≪ N` with no cancellation (`sobolev_trivial`), a
> shortfall of a full power of `N` from the Lindelöf target (`sobolev_shortfall`). Both effects — the
> `1/H`-free variation term and the off-diagonal saturation of the short mean square — push the same
> way.**

### C370 — the general form of the obstruction

The failure is structural rather than technical: **Sobolev is useless for a rapidly oscillating
function.** `F` oscillates at rate `\log N` in `t`, so `|F'| ≍ \log N·|F|` and the variation term can
never be smaller than the mean square. Any smoothing bridge of this type has the same defect.

This prices the campaign's own `SpikeSobolev` module honestly: it was built as the tool for exactly
this step, and Theorem 49 shows the step cannot be taken.

when `k > 1/δ` (`exceptional_empty_iff`).

> **`[THEOREM 53]` No finite moment order suffices uniformly: for every `k` there is a positive `δ` at
> which the exceptional set is not forced empty (`no_finite_moment_suffices`), and halving the excess
> doubles the required order (`requiredMomentOrder_diverges`). Emptying `E_δ` for **every** `δ > 0`
> therefore requires **all** moments — which is the Lindelöf hypothesis itself.**

### C380 — the sharpest form of the circularity barrier

This is the campaign's circularity mechanism at its limit. The moment framework is the only tool that
converts an average into an emptiness statement, and it does so **only at infinite order**, where the
input equals the conclusion.

> **Within the moment framework the pointwise/mean-value gap cannot be closed by any finite amount of
> averaging. A mechanism must therefore be *non-quantitative* in this respect: it must **classify**
> large values structurally rather than **count** them.**

### C381 — the specification, in final form

Combining C338 (S1–S8), Theorem 52 (scale-invariance) and Theorem 53:

> **A mechanism proving LH must (i) act on the pointwise statement directly, since the gap is

> resource outside the functional equation, whose three known instantiations are each blocked (D55,
> D56, D57).**

**Every clause is forced by a proved barrier.** The specification is now as tight as this campaign can
make it, and no known mathematical object satisfies it.

Axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; build green.

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.DirichletMVTWindow
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.LogPolyDirPoly

/-!
# Dirichlet mean value on a negative-frequency window

The direct smooth-AFE head uses `dirPoly N a (-t)`.  Coefficient conjugation reflects frequency,
so the existing arbitrary-window mean-value theorem transfers without changing coefficient energy.
-/

open Finset MeasureTheory intervalIntegral

namespace RHTower.Sieve

noncomputable section

/-- Mean-value theorem for the negative-frequency convention used by the
direct smooth-AFE head. -/
theorem dirichlet_meanValue_window_neg
    (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (T₁ T₂ : ℝ) :
    |(∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖dirPoly N a (-t)‖ ^ 2) -
        (T₂ - T₁) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2|
      ≤ 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2 := by
  have hpoint : ∀ t : ℝ,
      ‖dirPoly N a (-t)‖ ^ 2 =
        ‖dirPoly N (fun n => (starRingEnd ℂ) (a n)) t‖ ^ 2 := by
    intro t
    rw [dirPoly_conj_neg, RCLike.norm_conj]
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_congr (fun t _ => hpoint t)]
  have hbase :=
    dirichlet_meanValue_window N (fun n => (starRingEnd ℂ) (a n)) T₁ T₂
  have hcoeff :
      (∑ m : Fin N, ‖(starRingEnd ℂ) (a m)‖ ^ 2) =
        ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2 := by
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro m hm
    change ‖star (a m)‖ ^ 2 = _
    rw [norm_star]
  rwa [hcoeff] at hbase

end

end RHTower.Sieve

/-
The frontier object under the large sieve: the mean is exactly right, and only the maximum is open.

The frontier object is `Σ_(r) c_r e(n ξ_r)` over the `R ≍ N^(2/3)` Farey fractions of order
`L = N^(1/3)`, with unimodular coefficients and frequencies `ξ_r = √(2a/q)`.  The dual large sieve
gives

    Σ_(n ≤ N) |Σ_r c_r e(n ξ_r)|²  ≪  (N + δ^(-1)) Σ_r |c_r|² ,

where `δ` is the minimal spacing of the frequencies.  The spacing is `≫ L^(-2) = N^(-2/3)`, so
`δ^(-1) ≪ N^(2/3) ≪ N` and the mean square over `n ≤ N` is `≪ R = N^(2/3)`:

    **root mean square  ≪  N^(1/3)  —  exactly the Lindelöf value.**

So the across-arc half of the cancellation is available *in mean square*, and the entire deficit is
the passage from mean to maximum.  Quantitatively, at most `N^(1-2δ)` of the `N` values of `n` can
have the sum exceed `N^(1/3+δ)`.

On the other side, the resonance method gives a lower bound `≫ N^(1/3) exp(c√(log N log log N))`,
subpolynomially above the Lindelöf value.  So for the frontier object:

    mean square exponent        **2/3**   (root mean square **1/3**)
    known lower bound           **1/3**   up to `exp(c√(log N log log N))`
    trivial upper bound         **2/3**
    Lindelöf assertion          **1/3**

**Every known lower bound sits within a subpolynomial factor of the mean; the whole open interval is
the factor `N^(1/3)` between the mean and the trivial maximum.**
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.FourAccountings

namespace HTGeometry

/-! ### The sieve input -/

/-- Exponent of the number of Farey fractions of order `N^(1/3)`. -/
def frontierTermCount : ℚ := 2 / 3

/-- Exponent of the minimal spacing of the frontier frequencies (negative). -/
def frontierSpacing : ℚ := -(2 / 3)

/-- **The sieve's second term is dominated by the first.**  `δ^(-1) ≍ N^(2/3)` against `N`. -/
theorem sieve_second_term_negligible : -frontierSpacing < 1 := by
  unfold frontierSpacing; norm_num

/-- **The mean-square exponent delivered by the sieve.** -/
def frontierMeanSquare : ℚ := frontierTermCount

/-- **Its square root is exactly the Lindelöf value.** -/
theorem frontier_rms : frontierMeanSquare / 2 = 1 / 3 := by
  unfold frontierMeanSquare frontierTermCount; norm_num

/-! ### The three levels -/

/-- The trivial bound on the frontier object. -/
def frontierTrivial : ℚ := 2 / 3

/-- The Lindelöf assertion for the frontier object. -/
def frontierLindelof : ℚ := 1 / 3

/-- The root mean square, which the sieve delivers unconditionally. -/
def frontierRootMeanSquare : ℚ := 1 / 3

/-- **The root mean square already equals the Lindelöf value.** -/
theorem rms_equals_lindelof : frontierRootMeanSquare = frontierLindelof := rfl

/-- **And the trivial bound exceeds it by exactly the Farey order.** -/
theorem trivial_exceeds_lindelof : frontierTrivial - frontierLindelof = 1 / 3 := by
  unfold frontierTrivial frontierLindelof; norm_num

/-- That excess is one factor of the Farey order, matching the coherence deficit. -/
theorem excess_is_coherence_deficit :
    frontierTrivial - frontierLindelof = coherenceDeficit (1 / 3) := by
  rw [deficit_equals_scale, trivial_exceeds_lindelof]

/-! ### The exceptional set -/

/-- Exponent of the number of `n ≤ N` at which the sum can exceed `N^(1/3 + d)`. -/
def frontierExceptionalCount (d : ℚ) : ℚ := 1 - 2 * d

/-- **It is derived from the mean square.**  Values exceeding `N^(1/3+d)` contribute
`N^(2/3+2d)` each, against a total of `N^(1+2/3)`. -/
theorem exceptionalCount_from_meanSquare (d : ℚ) :
    frontierExceptionalCount d = 1 + frontierMeanSquare - (frontierMeanSquare + 2 * d) := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount; ring

/-- **The exceptional set shrinks as the excess grows.** -/
theorem exceptionalCount_antitone {d d' : ℚ} (h : d < d') :
    frontierExceptionalCount d' < frontierExceptionalCount d := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount; linarith

/-- **It vanishes only at `d = 1/2`**, far beyond the range in question. -/
theorem exceptionalCount_zero_iff (d : ℚ) : frontierExceptionalCount d = 0 ↔ d = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- At the trivial excess `d = 1/3` the exceptional set still has exponent `1/3`. -/
theorem exceptionalCount_at_trivial : frontierExceptionalCount (1 / 3) = 1 / 3 := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount; norm_num

/-! ### The two-sided position -/

/-- The known lower bound's exponent — the resonance method contributes only a subpolynomial
factor. -/
def frontierKnownLower : ℚ := 1 / 3

/-- **The known lower bound already matches the Lindelöf value in exponent.** -/
theorem lower_matches_lindelof : frontierKnownLower = frontierLindelof := rfl

/-- **So the whole open interval is between the mean and the trivial bound.** -/
theorem open_interval :
    frontierKnownLower = 1 / 3 ∧ frontierTrivial = 2 / 3 ∧
      frontierTrivial - frontierKnownLower = 1 / 3 := by
  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, ?_⟩
  unfold frontierTrivial frontierKnownLower; norm_num

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.CauchyIntegral
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.CircleAverage

/-!
# The Mean Value Property of Complex Differentiable Functions

This file established the classic mean value properties of complex differentiable functions,
computing the value of a function at the center of a circle as a circle average. It also provides
generalized versions that computing the value of a function at arbitrary points of a disk as circle
averages over suitable weighted functions.
-/

public section

open Complex Filter Function Metric Real Set Topology

variable
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E]
  {f : ℂ → E} {R : ℝ} {c w : ℂ} {s : Set ℂ}

/-!
## Generalized Mean Value Properties

For a complex differentiable function `f`, the theorems in this section compute values of `f` in the
interior of a disk as circle averages of a weighted function.
-/

/--
The **Generalized Mean Value Property** of complex differentiable functions: If `f : ℂ → E` is
continuous on a closed disc of radius `R` and center `c`, and is complex differentiable at all but
countably many points of its interior, then for every point `w` in the disk, the circle average
`circleAverage (fun z ↦ ((z - c) * (z - w)⁻¹) • f z) c R` equals `f w`.
-/
theorem circleAverage_sub_sub_inv_smul_of_differentiable_on_off_countable (hs : s.Countable)
    (h₁f : ContinuousOn f (closedBall c |R|)) (h₂f : ∀ z ∈ ball c |R| \ s, DifferentiableAt ℂ f z)
    (hw : w ∈ ball c |R|) :
    circleAverage (fun z ↦ ((z - c) / (z - w)) • f z) c R = f w := by
  rw [← circleAverage_abs_radius]
  rcases le_or_gt |R| 0 with hR | hR
  · simp_all [ball_eq_empty.2 hR]
  calc circleAverage (fun z ↦ ((z - c) * (z - w)⁻¹) • f z) c |R|
  _ = (2 * π * I)⁻¹ • (∮ z in C(c, |R|), (z - w)⁻¹ • f z) := by
    simp only [circleAverage_eq_circleIntegral hR.ne', mul_inv_rev, inv_I, neg_mul, neg_smul,
      neg_inj, ne_eq, mul_eq_zero, I_ne_zero, inv_eq_zero, ofReal_eq_zero, pi_ne_zero,
      OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, or_self, not_false_eq_true, smul_right_inj]
    apply circleIntegral.integral_congr hR.le
    intro z hz
    match_scalars
    have : z - c ≠ 0 := by grind [ne_of_mem_sphere]
    grind
  _ = f w := by
    rw [circleIntegral_sub_inv_smul_of_differentiable_on_off_countable hs hw h₁f h₂f]
    match_scalars
    simp [field]

/--
The **Generalized Mean Value Property** of complex differentiable functions: If `f : ℂ → E` is
complex differentiable at all points of a closed disc of radius `R` and center `c`, then for every
point `w` in the disk, the circle average `circleAverage (fun z ↦ ((z - c) * (z - w)⁻¹) • f z) c R`
equals `f w`.
-/
theorem DiffContOnCl.circleAverage_smul_div (hf : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (ball c |R|))
    (hw : w ∈ ball c |R|) :
    circleAverage (fun z ↦ ((z - c) / (z - w)) • f z) c R = f w := by
  by_cases hR : |R| ≤ 0
  · simp_all [ball_eq_empty.2 hR]
  apply circleAverage_sub_sub_inv_smul_of_differentiable_on_off_countable countable_empty _ _ hw
  · simpa [← closure_ball _ (ne_of_not_ge hR).symm] using hf.2
  · intro z hz
    rw [sdiff_empty] at hz
    apply (hf.1 z hz).differentiableAt (isOpen_ball.mem_nhds hz)

@[deprecated (since := "2026-02-11")]
alias circleAverage_sub_sub_inv_smul_of_differentiable_on := DiffContOnCl.circleAverage_smul_div

/-!
## Classic Mean Value Properties

For a complex differentiable function `f`, the theorems in this section compute value of `f` at the
center of a circle as a circle average of the function. This specializes the generalized mean value
properties discussed in the previous section.
-/

/--
The **Mean Value Property** of complex differentiable functions: If `f : ℂ → E` is continuous on a
closed disc of radius `R` and center `c`, and is complex differentiable at all but countably many
points of its interior, then the circle average `circleAverage f c R` equals `f c`.
-/
theorem circleAverage_of_differentiable_on_off_countable (hs : s.Countable)
    (h₁f : ContinuousOn f (closedBall c |R|)) (h₂f : ∀ z ∈ ball c |R| \ s, DifferentiableAt ℂ f z) :
    circleAverage f c R = f c := by
  by_cases hR : R = 0
  · simp [hR]
  · rw [← circleAverage_sub_sub_inv_smul_of_differentiable_on_off_countable hs h₁f h₂f (by aesop)]
    apply circleAverage_congr_sphere fun z hz ↦ ?_
    have : z - c ≠ 0 := by grind [ne_of_mem_sphere]
    simp_all

/--
The **Mean Value Property** of complex differentiable functions: If `f : ℂ → E` is complex
differentiable at all points of a closed disc of radius `R` and center `c`, then the circle average
`circleAverage f c R` equals `f c`.
-/
theorem DiffContOnCl.circleAverage (hf : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (ball c |R|)) :
    circleAverage f c R = f c := by
  by_cases hR : R = 0
  · simp [hR]
  · rw [← circleAverage_smul_div hf (by aesop)]
    apply circleAverage_congr_sphere fun z hz ↦ ?_

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.OffDiagonalBound

/-!
# The mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials

`|∫_0^T |F(t)|² dt - T ∑_{n < N} |a_n|²| ≤ 4N(1 + log N) ∑_{n < N} |a_n|²`

for `F(t) = ∑_{n < N} a_n n^{it}`.

The diagonal of the expanded mean square contributes `T ∑_n |a_n|²` exactly, and
`OffDiagonalBound.lean` bounds the rest.  The error `O(N log N)` is what the elementary comparison
between logarithmic and integer separations yields; the sharp `O(N)` of Montgomery and Vaughan needs
a Hilbert inequality at the frequencies `log n`, which the corpus does not own.
-/

namespace RHTower.Sieve

open Finset MeasureTheory

/-- **The mean value theorem, in complex form.** -/
theorem dirichlet_meanValue_complex (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (T : ℝ) :
    ‖(∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, ((‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))
        - (T : ℂ) * ∑ m : Fin N, ((‖a m‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)‖
      ≤ 4 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2 :=
  le_trans (norm_integral_normSq_dirPoly_sub_diag_le N a T) (offDiagonal_le N a)

/-- **The mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials.** -/
theorem dirichlet_meanValue_theorem (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (T : ℝ) :
    |(∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2) - T * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2|
      ≤ 4 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2 := by
  have hbase := dirichlet_meanValue_complex N a T
  have hcast : (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, ((‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))
      - (T : ℂ) * ∑ m : Fin N, ((‖a m‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)
      = ((((∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2) - T * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2 : ℝ)) : ℂ) := by
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_ofReal, ← Complex.ofReal_sum, ← Complex.ofReal_mul,
      ← Complex.ofReal_sub]
  rw [hcast, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs] at hbase
  exact hbase

end RHTower.Sieve

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.DirichletMVT

/-!
# The Dirichlet mean value theorem on a window

`DirichletMVT.lean` proves the mean value theorem anchored at `0`.  Every moment computation on a
dyadic window `[T, 2T]` needs it there instead.  Subtracting the two anchored statements doubles the
error and keeps the exact main term `(T₂ − T₁)·∑|a_n|²`.
-/

open Finset MeasureTheory intervalIntegral


namespace RHTower.Sieve

noncomputable section

theorem continuous_normSq_dirPoly (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2 := by
  have hc : Continuous (dirPoly N a) := by
    unfold dirPoly
    refine continuous_finsetSum _ fun n _ => ?_
    exact continuous_const.mul
      (Complex.continuous_exp.comp
        ((Complex.continuous_ofReal.comp
          (continuous_id.mul continuous_const)).mul continuous_const))
  exact hc.norm.pow 2

theorem intervalIntegrable_normSq_dirPoly (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (u v : ℝ) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2) volume u v :=
  (continuous_normSq_dirPoly N a).intervalIntegrable u v

/-- **The mean value theorem on an arbitrary window.**  Subtracting the two anchored
mean values doubles the error but keeps the exact main term `(T₂ − T₁)·∑|a|²`. -/
theorem dirichlet_meanValue_window (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (T₁ T₂ : ℝ) :
    |(∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2) - (T₂ - T₁) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2|
      ≤ 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2 := by
  have h₁ := dirichlet_meanValue_theorem N a T₁
  have h₂ := dirichlet_meanValue_theorem N a T₂
  have hsplit : (∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2)
      = (∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T₂, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2)
        - ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T₁, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_left
      (intervalIntegrable_normSq_dirPoly N a 0 T₂)
      (intervalIntegrable_normSq_dirPoly N a 0 T₁)]
  rw [hsplit]
  have hrw : (∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T₂, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2)
        - (∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T₁, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2)
        - (T₂ - T₁) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2
      = ((∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T₂, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2) - T₂ * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2)
        - ((∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T₁, ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2) - T₁ * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2) := by
    ring
  rw [hrw]
  refine le_trans (abs_sub _ _) ?_
  linarith

/-- **The dyadic mean value theorem.** -/
theorem dirichlet_meanValue_dyadic (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (T : ℝ) :
    |(∫ t in T..(2 * T), ‖dirPoly N a t‖ ^ 2) - T * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2|
      ≤ 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) * ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ 2 := by
  have h := dirichlet_meanValue_window N a T (2 * T)
  have hrw : 2 * T - T = T := by ring
  rwa [hrw] at h

end

end RHTower.Sieve

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.SeibergWitten.FlatClifford
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.SeibergWitten.Connections

/-!
# Flat chiral Dirac contraction

This module turns the verified flat chiral Clifford matrices into the contraction required by the
mathlib `CovariantDerivative` interface.  Given any genuine covariant derivative on the constant
positive spinor bundle over Euclidean four-space, `flatChiralDirac` is its chiral Dirac operator.
The displayed formula is the finite sum of Clifford multiplication by the four coordinate basis
vectors applied to the covariant derivative in that direction.

No particular covariant derivative is asserted to exist here: this module provides the exact
Dirac construction once such a geometric connection is supplied.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.SeibergWitten

/-- Coordinate basis vector of Euclidean four-space. -/
def flatFourBasis (i : Fin 4) : FourSpace :=
  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin 4) ℝ).symm (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4) i)

/-- Clifford contraction of a one-form with values in the flat positive spinor bundle. -/
def flatCliffordContraction :
    CliffordContractionData FourSpace flatPositiveSpinorBundle flatNegativeSpinorBundle where
  contract := fun _ derivative =>
    ∑ i, flatCliffordPlus (flatFourBasis i) (derivative (flatFourBasis i))

/-- Chiral Dirac operator induced by any smooth connection on the flat positive spinor bundle. -/
def flatChiralDirac
    (connection : SmoothSpinorConnection FourSpace flatPositiveSpinorBundle)
    (sigma : ∀ x, flatPositiveSpinorBundle x) : ∀ x, flatNegativeSpinorBundle x :=
  connection.dirac flatCliffordContraction sigma

/-- Coordinate formula for the flat chiral Dirac contraction. -/
theorem flatChiralDirac_apply
    (connection : SmoothSpinorConnection FourSpace flatPositiveSpinorBundle)
    (sigma : ∀ x, flatPositiveSpinorBundle x) (x : FourSpace) :
    flatChiralDirac connection sigma x =
      ∑ i, flatCliffordPlus (flatFourBasis i)
        (connection.covariantDerivative sigma x (flatFourBasis i)) :=
  rfl

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.SeibergWitten

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.SeibergWitten.FlatDirac

/-!
# Flat spinor connection on Euclidean four-space

The constant positive spinor bundle has a closed covariant derivative in mathlib: in its global
trivialization, differentiate the coefficient function by `mvfderiv`.  The only geometric bridge
needed for the Leibniz laws is that differentiability of a section of a trivial vector bundle is
equivalent to differentiability of its fiber-valued coefficient function.

Consequently, constant spinors are parallel and their chiral Dirac image is zero.  This is a
genuine connection on the smooth flat bundle, while remaining a flat Euclidean model rather than
a construction on every oriented four-manifold.
-/

noncomputable section

open scoped Manifold

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.SeibergWitten

/-- A differentiable section of a trivial flat bundle has a differentiable coefficient function in
its global trivialization. -/
private theorem mdifferentiableAt_of_flatTrivialSection
    (F : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    {sigma : ∀ x, Bundle.Trivial FourSpace F x} {x : FourSpace}
    (hsigma : MDifferentiableAt fourModel (fourModel.prod 𝓘(ℝ, F)) (fun y =>
      (⟨y, sigma y⟩ : Bundle.TotalSpace F (Bundle.Trivial FourSpace F))) x) :
    MDifferentiableAt fourModel 𝓘(ℝ, F) sigma x := by
  letI : MemTrivializationAtlas (Bundle.Trivial.trivialization FourSpace F) :=
    ⟨by change Bundle.Trivial.trivialization FourSpace F ∈
      {Bundle.Trivial.trivialization FourSpace F}; simp⟩
  have htotal :=
    ((Bundle.Trivial.trivialization FourSpace F).mdifferentiableAt_totalSpace_iff
      fourModel (fun y => (⟨y, sigma y⟩ : Bundle.TotalSpace F
        (Bundle.Trivial FourSpace F))) (by simp)).mp hsigma
  simpa using htotal.2

/-- Standard flat covariant derivative on every constant real normed vector bundle. -/
noncomputable def flatTrivialCovariantDerivative
    (F : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] :
    CovariantDerivative fourModel F (Bundle.Trivial FourSpace F) where
  toFun := fun sigma => mvfderiv fourModel sigma
  isCovariantDerivativeOnUniv := by
    constructor
    · intro sigma tau x hsigma htau _
      change MDifferentiableAt fourModel (fourModel.prod 𝓘(ℝ, F))
        (fun y => (⟨y, sigma y⟩ : Bundle.TotalSpace F (Bundle.Trivial FourSpace F))) x at hsigma
      change MDifferentiableAt fourModel (fourModel.prod 𝓘(ℝ, F))
        (fun y => (⟨y, tau y⟩ : Bundle.TotalSpace F (Bundle.Trivial FourSpace F))) x at htau
      simpa only [Pi.add_apply] using
        mvfderiv_add (mdifferentiableAt_of_flatTrivialSection F hsigma)
          (mdifferentiableAt_of_flatTrivialSection F htau)
    · intro sigma g x hsigma hg _
      change MDifferentiableAt fourModel (fourModel.prod 𝓘(ℝ, F))
        (fun y => (⟨y, sigma y⟩ : Bundle.TotalSpace F (Bundle.Trivial FourSpace F))) x at hsigma
      exact mvfderiv_smul hg (mdifferentiableAt_of_flatTrivialSection F hsigma)

/-- Standard flat covariant derivative on the constant positive spinor bundle. -/
noncomputable def flatPositiveSpinorCovariantDerivative :
    CovariantDerivative fourModel (Fin 2 → ℂ) flatPositiveSpinorBundle :=
  flatTrivialCovariantDerivative (Fin 2 → ℂ)

/-- Standard flat covariant derivative on the constant negative spinor bundle. -/
noncomputable def flatNegativeSpinorCovariantDerivative :
    CovariantDerivative fourModel (Fin 2 → ℂ) flatNegativeSpinorBundle :=
  flatTrivialCovariantDerivative (Fin 2 → ℂ)

/-- Standard flat covariant derivative on the determinant line of the flat Spinᶜ bundle. -/
noncomputable def flatDeterminantLineCovariantDerivative :
    CovariantDerivative fourModel ℂ flatDeterminantLineBundle :=
  flatTrivialCovariantDerivative ℂ

/-- The actual flat positive-spinor connection. -/
noncomputable def flatPositiveSpinorConnection :
    SmoothSpinorConnection FourSpace flatPositiveSpinorBundle where
  covariantDerivative := flatPositiveSpinorCovariantDerivative

/-- The actual flat negative-spinor connection. -/
noncomputable def flatNegativeSpinorConnection :
    SmoothSpinorConnection FourSpace flatNegativeSpinorBundle where
  covariantDerivative := flatNegativeSpinorCovariantDerivative

/-- Joint flat connection data on the positive and negative spinor bundles and determinant line.
This is the vector-bundle connection prelude induced by the trivial flat Spinᶜ model; integrating

  negative : SmoothSpinorConnection FourSpace flatNegativeSpinorBundle

noncomputable def flatSpinCConnectionPrelude : FlatSpinCConnectionPrelude where
  positive := flatPositiveSpinorConnection
  negative := flatNegativeSpinorConnection

/-!
# The flat profile in the physical chart, and the logistic kernel

In the physical chart `s = e^{-L}` the flat profile `u(s) = F(-log s)` has square-integrable value
and non-square-integrable derivative: the two ray integrals

`∫ exp (-2√L) exp (-L) dL < ∞`,   `∫ exp (L - 2√L) / L dL = ∞`

decide membership, and the second diverges because `L - 2√L - log L → ∞`.  So the profile lies in
the completed boundary class and outside the raw spatial derivative domain.

The logistic kernel `k(y) = e^y/(1+e^y)^2` — the `L`-derivative of the Carleman cutoff factor —
is a probability density: its antiderivative is `-(1+e^y)⁻¹`.
-/

open Set MeasureTheory Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The physical-chart square of the flat profile. -/
def flatPortValueDensity (L : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-2 * Real.sqrt L) * Real.exp (-L)

/-- The physical-chart square of the flat profile's spatial derivative. -/
def flatPortDerivativeDensity (L : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp (L - 2 * Real.sqrt L) / L

/-- **`(14)`: the flat profile is square integrable on the physical ray.** -/
theorem integrableOn_flatPortValueDensity :
    IntegrableOn flatPortValueDensity (Ioi (1:ℝ)) volume := by
  have hmajor : IntegrableOn (fun L : ℝ => Real.exp (-L)) (Ioi (1:ℝ)) volume :=
    integrableOn_exp_neg_Ioi 1
  refine Integrable.mono' hmajor ?_ ?_
  · apply Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable
    unfold flatPortValueDensity
    fun_prop
  · filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioi] with L hL
    have hLpos : (0:ℝ) < L := lt_trans zero_lt_one hL
    have hsq : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt L := Real.sqrt_nonneg L
    have h1 : Real.exp (-2 * Real.sqrt L) ≤ 1 := Real.exp_le_one_iff.mpr (by linarith)
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, flatPortValueDensity,
      abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0:ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (-2 * Real.sqrt L) * Real.exp (-L))]
    nlinarith [Real.exp_pos (-L), Real.exp_pos (-2 * Real.sqrt L)]

/-- The physical derivative density blows up: the flat profile is beyond `H¹`. -/
theorem tendsto_flatPortDerivativeDensity :
    Tendsto flatPortDerivativeDensity atTop atTop := by
  have hlogsqrt : ∀ L : ℝ, 0 < L → Real.log L ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt L := by
    intro L hL
    have hs : 0 < Real.sqrt L := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hL
    have hlog : Real.log (Real.sqrt L) ≤ Real.sqrt L - 1 := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos hs
    have hsq : Real.log L = 2 * Real.log (Real.sqrt L) := by
      have h : Real.sqrt L ^ 2 = L := Real.sq_sqrt hL.le
      calc Real.log L = Real.log (Real.sqrt L ^ 2) := by rw [h]
        _ = 2 * Real.log (Real.sqrt L) := by rw [Real.log_pow]; norm_num
    rw [hsq]
    linarith
  have hev : ∀ᶠ L : ℝ in atTop, L / 2 ≤ L - 2 * Real.sqrt L - Real.log L := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (64:ℝ)] with L hL
    have hLpos : (0:ℝ) < L := by linarith
    have h4 : (8:ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt L := by
      have : Real.sqrt 64 ≤ Real.sqrt L := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hL
      rwa [show (64:ℝ) = 8 ^ 2 by norm_num, Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)] at this
    have hsq : Real.sqrt L * Real.sqrt L = L := Real.mul_self_sqrt hLpos.le
    have hlog := hlogsqrt L hLpos
    nlinarith [Real.sqrt_nonneg L]
  have hhalf : Tendsto (fun L : ℝ => L / 2) atTop atTop :=
    tendsto_id.atTop_div_const (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) < 2)
  have hinner : Tendsto (fun L : ℝ => L - 2 * Real.sqrt L - Real.log L) atTop atTop :=
    tendsto_atTop_mono' atTop hev hhalf
  have hexp : Tendsto (fun L : ℝ => Real.exp (L - 2 * Real.sqrt L - Real.log L)) atTop atTop :=
    Real.tendsto_exp_atTop.comp hinner
  refine hexp.congr' ?_
  filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0:ℝ)] with L hL
  rw [flatPortDerivativeDensity, Real.exp_sub, Real.exp_log hL]

/-- **`(13)`: the flat profile's spatial derivative is not square integrable.** -/
theorem not_integrableOn_flatPortDerivativeDensity :
    ¬ IntegrableOn flatPortDerivativeDensity (Ioi (1:ℝ)) volume :=
  not_integrableOn_Ioi_of_tendsto_atTop tendsto_flatPortDerivativeDensity 1

/-- The logistic kernel `k(y) = e^y/(1+e^y)^2`. -/
def logisticKernel (y : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp y / (1 + Real.exp y) ^ 2

theorem logisticKernel_pos (y : ℝ) : 0 < logisticKernel y := by
  have hy := Real.exp_pos y
  unfold logisticKernel
  positivity

theorem continuous_logisticKernel : Continuous logisticKernel := by
  unfold logisticKernel
  have h : ∀ y : ℝ, (1 + Real.exp y) ^ 2 ≠ 0 := by
    intro y
    have := Real.exp_pos y
    positivity
  fun_prop (disch := intro y; exact h y)

/-- The logistic primitive `-(1+e^y)⁻¹`. -/
def logisticPrimitive (y : ℝ) : ℝ := -(1 + Real.exp y)⁻¹

theorem hasDerivAt_logisticPrimitive (y : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt logisticPrimitive (logisticKernel y) y := by
  have hpos : (0:ℝ) < 1 + Real.exp y := by
    have := Real.exp_pos y
    linarith
  have hne : (1 + Real.exp y) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hpos
  have hbase : HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => 1 + Real.exp x) (Real.exp y) y := by
    have := (Real.hasDerivAt_exp y).const_add (1:ℝ)
    simpa using this

tCast_eq (by omega)]

/-- **The reflection curvature** of a carrier `F`: the second logarithmic derivative of its reflection
cocycle, `κ_F = deriv (logDeriv (reflCocycle F))`.  It is the tier-two weld invariant: it annihilates
every pure-conductor cocycle and detects genuinely archimedean welds. -/
def reflCurvature (F : ℂ → ℂ) : ℂ → ℂ := deriv (logDeriv (reflCocycle F))

/-- **The conductor cocycle is curvature-flat.**  For `Q ≥ 2` the reflection curvature of the
conductor cocycle vanishes identically: its logarithmic derivative is the constant `2·log Q`, whose
derivative is `0`.  Exact-conductor members carry no tier-two (archimedean) weld — their whole datum
is the rate `2 log Q`, already read by the rate lattice. -/
theorem conductorCocycle_curvature_zero {Q : ℕ} (hQ : 2 ≤ Q) :
    deriv (logDeriv (conductorCocycle Q)) = (0 : ℂ → ℂ) := by
  have hconst : logDeriv (conductorCocycle Q) = (fun _ : ℂ => 2 * (Real.log Q : ℂ)) := by
    funext s; exact conductorCocycle_logDeriv hQ s
  rw [hconst]; funext s; simp

/-- **An exact-conductor member is curvature-flat where it is nonzero.** If `f` satisfies the
degree-zero equation `f s = Q^{1−2s}·f(1−s)` and is nonvanishing on an open set `U`, its
reflection cocycle agrees with the conductor cocycle throughout `U`, so on `U` the two logarithmic
derivatives coincide.  Combined with `conductorCocycle_curvature_zero`, the reflection curvature of `f`
vanishes on `U`: exact conductors sit on the flat locus of the curvature invariant. -/
theorem reflCocycle_eqOn_conductorCocycle {f : ℂ → ℂ} {Q : ℕ}
    (hfe : ∀ s, f s = (Q : ℂ) ^ (1 - 2 * s) * f (1 - s)) {U : Set ℂ} (hU : ∀ s ∈ U, f s ≠ 0) :
    Set.EqOn (reflCocycle f) (conductorCocycle Q) U := by
  intro s hs
  rw [conductorCocycle, reflCocycle_of_conductor hfe (hU s hs)]

end RHTower

/-!
# Flat Kerr--Newman Killing wave operator for the Xi mass profile

The zero mass--spin--charge Kerr--Newman stationary block is the flat Lorentz plane. At closed
unit mass and damping parameters, the existing Xi mass Klein--Gordon equation becomes a wave
operator eigen-equation after contraction with that block. This is only a sign and operator
correspondence: it does not identify RHTower and Boyer--Lindquist coordinates, calculate a curved
wave operator, or imply RH.
-/

namespace RHTower

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- Unit mass/damping member of the existing Xi spectral-cross profile family. -/
noncomputable def xiMassUnitProfile (u h : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  xiMassSpectralCrossMoment 1 1 u 0 h

/-- Scalar wave operator contracted with the flat Kerr--Newman stationary Killing block. -/
noncomputable def kerrNewmanFlatKillingWaveOperator (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ) (u h : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  (kerrNewmanKillingBlock 0 0 0 1 (Real.pi / 2) 0 0 : ℂ) *
      deriv (deriv (fun v : ℝ => f v h)) u +
    (kerrNewmanKillingBlock 0 0 0 1 (Real.pi / 2) 1 1 : ℂ) *
      deriv (deriv (fun v : ℝ => f u v)) h

/-- The flat Kerr--Newman block supplies the Lorentzian principal signs `(-,+)`. -/
theorem kerrNewmanFlatKillingWaveOperator_eq
    (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ) (u h : ℝ) :
    kerrNewmanFlatKillingWaveOperator f u h =
      -deriv (deriv (fun v : ℝ => f v h)) u +
        deriv (deriv (fun v : ℝ => f u v)) h := by
  unfold kerrNewmanFlatKillingWaveOperator
  rw [belinskiZakharov_flatKillingBlock]
  norm_num

/-- The unit Xi mass profile is an eigenfunction of the flat Kerr--Newman Killing wave operator. -/
theorem xiMassUnitProfile_kerrNewmanFlatKillingWave
    (u h : ℝ) :
    kerrNewmanFlatKillingWaveOperator xiMassUnitProfile u h =
      xiMassUnitProfile u h := by
  change kerrNewmanFlatKillingWaveOperator
      (fun u h => xiMassSpectralCrossMoment 1 1 u 0 h) u h =
        xiMassSpectralCrossMoment 1 1 u 0 h
  rw [kerrNewmanFlatKillingWaveOperator_eq]
  have hkg := xiMassProfile_kleinGordon (a := 1) (σ := 1) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) u h
  simp_rw [xiMassSpectralCrossMoment_zero] at hkg ⊢
  have hspace : xiMassSpectralCrossMoment 1 1 u 0 =
      fun v => xiMassSpectralCrossProfile 1 1 u v := by
    funext v
    exact xiMassSpectralCrossMoment_zero 1 1 u v
  rw [hspace] at hkg
  norm_num at hkg
  linear_combination -hkg

/-- The prime-tail position profile in the RH criterion is the coordinate-weighted unit
Kerr--Newman wave profile. -/
theorem xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfile_unit_eq_kerrNewmanFlatWave
    (u : ℝ) :
    xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfile 1 1 u =
      fun h : ℝ => (h : ℂ) * xiMassUnitProfile u h := by
  funext h
  rfl

/-- The prime-tail profile used in the RH current has the stated first coordinate derivative. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_kerrNewmanFlatXiMassWeightedProfile
    (u h : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun q : ℝ => (q : ℂ) * xiMassUnitProfile u q)
      (xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfileDeriv 1 1 u h) h := by
  change HasDerivAt (xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfile 1 1 u)
    (xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfileDeriv 1 1 u h) h
  exact hasDerivAt_xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfile (a := 1) (sigma := 1)
    (by norm_num) (by norm_num) u h

/-- The derivative from the coordinate-weighted flat Kerr--Newman profile has the exact second
derivative used to define the prime-tail Green current. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_kerrNewmanFlatXiMassWeightedProfileDeriv
    (u h : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfileDeriv 1 1 u)
      (xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfileSecond 1 1 u h) h :=
  hasDerivAt_xiMassPrimeTailPositionProfileDeriv (a := 1) (sigma := 1)
    (by norm_num) (by norm_num) u h

/-- The prime-tail Green current used by the Xi-mass criterion, specialized to the same unit
profile that solves the flat Kerr--Newman wave equation. -/
noncomputable def kerrNewmanFlatXiMassPrimeTailGreenCurrent (u : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  xiMassCriticalPrimeTailGreenCurrent 1 1 u

/-- **Exact RH interface.** RH is equivalent to uniform boundedness of the prime-tail
Green--Stokes current driven by the coordinate-weighted unit flat Kerr--Newman wave profile.

The preceding wave equation alone gives no such bound: the prime-tail source is the indispensable
arithmetic input. -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_iff_kerrNewmanFlatXiMassPrimeTailGreenCurrentLineBound :
    RiemannHypothesis ↔
      ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u →
        ‖kerrNewmanFlatXiMassPrimeTailGreenCurrent u‖ ≤ C := by
  simpa [kerrNewmanFlatXiMassPrimeTailGreenCurrent] using
    (riemannHypothesis_iff_xiMassCriticalPrimeTailGreenCurrentLineBound
      (a := 1) (sigma := 1) (by norm_num) (by norm_num))

end RHTower

    (g := Set.indicator {-1, 0} 1)

    simp_rw [ofReal_mul, this, ← smul_eq_mul]
    apply Summable.const_smul
    apply Summable.const_smul
    rw [summable_jacobiTheta₂_term_iff]
    simp

      rw [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]

      apply tendsto_zero_iff_norm_tendsto_zero.mpr

      exact neg_one_lt_zero.trans (by positivity)

theorem tendsto_gaussianCooledMoment (J : ℝ → ℝ) (hJc : Continuous J)
    {C : ℝ} (hJb : ∀ x, |J x| ≤ C) (m : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun tau : ℝ => ∫ y, y ^ m * Real.exp (-y ^ 2) * J ((Real.sqrt tau)⁻¹ * y)) atTop
      (𝓝 ((∫ y, y ^ m * Real.exp (-y ^ 2)) * J 0))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendsto_gaussianCooledMoment (J : ℝ → ℝ) (hJc : Continuous J)
    {C : ℝ} (hJb : ∀ x, |J x| ≤ C) (m : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun tau : ℝ => ∫ y, y ^ m * Real.exp (-y ^ 2) * J ((Real.sqrt tau)⁻¹ * y)) atTop
      (𝓝 ((∫ y, y ^ m * Real.exp (-y ^ 2)) * J 0))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  set g : ℝ → ℝ := fun y => y ^ m * Real.exp (-y ^ 2) with hg
  have hgc : Continuous g :=
    (continuous_pow m).mul (Real.continuous_exp.comp (continuous_neg.comp (continuous_pow 2)))
  have hgint : Integrable g := integrable_pow_mul_exp_neg_sq m
  rw [← integral_mul_const]
  apply tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence (fun y => C * ‖g y‖)
  · filter_upwards with tau
    exact (hgc.mul (hJc.comp (continuous_const.mul continuous_id))).aestronglyMeasurable
  · filter_upwards with tau
    filter_upwards with y
    rw [norm_mul]
    calc ‖g y‖ * ‖J ((Real.sqrt tau)⁻¹ * y)‖ ≤ ‖g y‖ * C := by
            refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (norm_nonneg _)
            rw [Real.norm_eq_abs]; exact hJb _
      _ = C * ‖g y‖ := mul_comm _ _
  · exact hgint.norm.const_mul C
  · filter_upwards with y
    have hpt : Tendsto (fun tau : ℝ => J ((Real.sqrt tau)⁻¹ * y)) atTop (𝓝 (J 0)) := by
      have h0 : Tendsto (fun tau : ℝ => (Real.sqrt tau)⁻¹ * y) atTop (𝓝 (0 * y)) :=
        Tendsto.mul_const y ((Real.tendsto_sqrt_atTop.comp tendsto_id).inv_tendsto_atTop)
      rw [zero_mul] at h0
      exact (hJc.tendsto 0).comp h0
    exact hpt.const_mul (g y)

theorem reciprocalPacketProjection_strong_tendsto_id
    (F : ReciprocalPacketExhaustion) (x : PrimeHodgeHistoryHilbert) :
    Tendsto (fun n => reciprocalPacketProjection (F.packet n) x)
      atTop (nhds x)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem reciprocalPacketProjection_strong_tendsto_id
    (F : ReciprocalPacketExhaustion) (x : PrimeHodgeHistoryHilbert) :
    Tendsto (fun n => reciprocalPacketProjection (F.packet n) x)
      atTop (nhds x)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let f : ℕ → PrimeHodgeHistoryIndex → ℝ := fun n i =>
    ‖(reciprocalPacketProjection (F.packet n) x - x) i‖ ^ 2
  let bound : PrimeHodgeHistoryIndex → ℝ := fun i => ‖x i‖ ^ 2
  have hbound : Summable bound := by
    simpa [bound] using (lp.memℓp x).summable (by norm_num)
  have hpoint : ∀ i, Tendsto (fun n => f n i) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    intro i
    obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := F.eventually_mem i
    refine tendsto_const_nhds.congr' ?_
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop N] with n hn
    simp [f, reciprocalPacketProjection_apply, hN n hn]
  have hdom : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ i, ‖f n i‖ ≤ bound i := by
    refine Eventually.of_forall fun n i => ?_
    classical
    by_cases hi : i ∈ F.packet n
    · simp [f, bound, reciprocalPacketProjection_apply, hi]
    · simp [f, bound, reciprocalPacketProjection_apply, hi]
  have htsum : Tendsto (fun n => ∑' i, f n i) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    simpa using tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence hbound hpoint hdom
  have hsq : ∀ n,
      ‖reciprocalPacketProjection (F.packet n) x - x‖ ^ 2 = ∑' i, f n i := by
    intro n
    simpa [f] using HilbertSchmidt.lp_norm_sq_eq
      (reciprocalPacketProjection (F.packet n) x - x)
  have hsqrt := Real.continuous_sqrt.continuousAt.tendsto.comp htsum
  have hnorm : Tendsto
      (fun n => ‖reciprocalPacketProjection (F.packet n) x - x‖)
      atTop (nhds 0) := by
    have hsqrt' : Tendsto (fun n => Real.sqrt (∑' i, f n i))
        atTop (nhds 0) := by simpa [Function.comp_def] using hsqrt
    convert hsqrt' using 1
    funext n
    rw [← hsq n, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)]
  rw [tendsto_iff_dist_tendsto_zero]
  simpa only [dist_eq_norm] using hnorm

source_arguments.statement:
theorem opTrace_comp_tendsto_of_strong_tendsto_of_uniform_bound
    {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot]
    {Aι : ι → H →L[ℂ] H} {A T : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hT : T.IsTraceClass) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hbound : ∀ᶠ n in l, ‖Aι n‖ ≤ C)
    (hstrong : ∀ x, Tendsto (fun n => Aι n x) l (𝓝 (A x))) :
    Tendsto (fun n => opTrace (Aι n ∘L T)) l
      (𝓝 (opTrace (A ∘L T)))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem opTrace_comp_tendsto_of_strong_tendsto_of_uniform_bound
    {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot]
    {Aι : ι → H →L[ℂ] H} {A T : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hT : T.IsTraceClass) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hbound : ∀ᶠ n in l, ‖Aι n‖ ≤ C)
    (hstrong : ∀ x, Tendsto (fun n => Aι n x) l (𝓝 (A x))) :
    Tendsto (fun n => opTrace (Aι n ∘L T)) l
      (𝓝 (opTrace (A ∘L T)))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨S, U, hS, hU, hfac⟩ := hT
  let b := hsBasis ℂ H
  let f := fun n i =>
    inner ℂ (adjoint U (b i)) (Aι n (S (b i)))
  let g := fun i =>
    inner ℂ (adjoint U (b i)) (A (S (b i)))
  let bound := fun i =>
    (C / 2) * (‖adjoint U (b i)‖ ^ 2 + ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)
  have hboundSummable : Summable bound := by
    have hsum := (hU.adjoint.summable b).add (hS.summable b)
    have hscaled := Summable.mul_left (C / 2) hsum
    simpa only [bound] using hscaled
  have hpoint : ∀ i, Tendsto (fun n => f n i) l (𝓝 (g i)) := by
    intro i
    exact ((innerSL ℂ (adjoint U (b i))).continuous.tendsto
      (A (S (b i)))).comp (hstrong (S (b i)))
  have hdom : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ i, ‖f n i‖ ≤ bound i := by
    filter_upwards [hbound] with n hn i
    have hinner := norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℂ)
      (adjoint U (b i)) (Aι n (S (b i)))
    have hop := (Aι n).le_opNorm (S (b i))
    have hAS : ‖Aι n (S (b i))‖ ≤ C * ‖S (b i)‖ :=
      hop.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hn (norm_nonneg _))
    calc
      ‖f n i‖ ≤ ‖adjoint U (b i)‖ * ‖Aι n (S (b i))‖ := hinner
      _ ≤ ‖adjoint U (b i)‖ * (C * ‖S (b i)‖) := by
        gcongr
      _ ≤ bound i := by
        dsimp only [bound]
        have hu : 0 ≤ ‖adjoint U (b i)‖ := norm_nonneg _
        have hs : 0 ≤ ‖S (b i)‖ := norm_nonneg _
        nlinarith [sq_nonneg (‖adjoint U (b i)‖ - ‖S (b i)‖)]
  have htsum := tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence
    hboundSummable hpoint hdom
  have hstage (n : ι) :
      opTrace (Aι n ∘L T) = ∑' i, f n i := by
    calc
      opTrace (Aι n ∘L T) = opTrace ((Aι n ∘L S) ∘L U) := by
        rw [hfac, comp_assoc]
      _ = opTrace (U ∘L (Aι n ∘L S)) :=
        opTrace_comp_comm (hS.comp_left (Aι n)) hU
      _ = ∑' i, inner ℂ (b i) ((U ∘L (Aι n ∘L S)) (b i)) :=
        opTrace_comp_eq_tsum_basis hU (hS.comp_left (Aι n)) b
      _ = ∑' i, f n i := by
        apply tsum_congr
        intro i
        rw [inner_comp_apply]
        rfl
  have hlimit : opTrace (A ∘L T) = ∑' i, g i := by
    calc

    (hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable g semilocalArchimedeanGammaMeasure)
    {w : ℂ} (hw : ‖w‖ < 1 / 4) :
    HasSum (fun m : ℕ => ∫ s : ℝ, (mpCoefficient s m : ℂ) * w ^ m * g s
        ∂semilocalArchimedeanGammaMeasure)

theorem hasSum_integral_mpCoefficient_mul {g : ℝ → ℂ}
    (hg : Integrable (fun s : ℝ => Real.exp (|s| / 2) * ‖g s‖) semilocalArchimedeanGammaMeasure)
    (hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable g semilocalArchimedeanGammaMeasure)
    {w : ℂ} (hw : ‖w‖ < 1 / 4) :
    HasSum (fun m : ℕ => ∫ s : ℝ, (mpCoefficient s m : ℂ) * w ^ m * g s
        ∂semilocalArchimedeanGammaMeasure)
      (∫ s : ℝ, mpGeneratingFunction s w * g s ∂semilocalArchimedeanGammaMeasure)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  set C : ℝ := (3 / 4 : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) with hC
  have hC0 : 0 ≤ C := by positivity
  have hr0 : 0 ≤ 4 * ‖w‖ := by positivity
  have hr1 : 4 * ‖w‖ < 1 := by linarith
  refine hasSum_integral_of_dominated_convergence
    (fun m s => C * Real.exp (|s| / 2) * ‖g s‖ * (4 * ‖w‖) ^ m) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro m
    exact (((Complex.continuous_ofReal.comp (continuous_mpCoefficient m)).mul
      continuous_const).aestronglyMeasurable).mul hmeas
  · intro m
    filter_upwards with s
    rw [norm_mul, norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, norm_pow]
    have h := abs_mpCoefficient_le s m
    calc |mpCoefficient s m| * ‖w‖ ^ m * ‖g s‖
        ≤ (C * Real.exp (|s| / 2) * 4 ^ m) * ‖w‖ ^ m * ‖g s‖ :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h (by positivity))
            (norm_nonneg _)
      _ = C * Real.exp (|s| / 2) * ‖g s‖ * (4 * ‖w‖) ^ m := by rw [mul_pow]; ring
  · filter_upwards with s
    exact (summable_geometric_of_lt_one hr0 hr1).mul_left _
  · have hfun : (fun s : ℝ => ∑' m : ℕ, C * Real.exp (|s| / 2) * ‖g s‖ * (4 * ‖w‖) ^ m) =
        fun s : ℝ => (C * (1 - 4 * ‖w‖)⁻¹) * (Real.exp (|s| / 2) * ‖g s‖) := by
      funext s
      rw [tsum_mul_left, tsum_geometric_of_lt_one hr0 hr1]
      ring
    rw [hfun]
    exact hg.const_mul _
  · filter_upwards with s
    exact (hasSum_mpGeneratingFunction s (hw.trans (by norm_num))).mul_right (g s)

    rw [show (∫ u : ℝ, f u) = ∫ u : ℝ in Ici 1, (u : ℂ) ^ (-s) by

theorem tendsto_entireDet2_of_hsNorm_sub_tendsto_zero
    (K : ℕ → ι × ι → ℂ) (K₀ : ι × ι → ℂ)
    (hK : ∀ n, IsHS (K n)) (hK₀ : IsHS K₀)
    (hlim : Tendsto (fun n => hsNorm (K n - K₀)) atTop (nhds 0))
    (z : ℂ) :
    Tendsto (fun n => entireDet2 (K n) z) atTop (nhds (entireDet2 K₀ z))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendsto_entireDet2_of_hsNorm_sub_tendsto_zero
    (K : ℕ → ι × ι → ℂ) (K₀ : ι × ι → ℂ)
    (hK : ∀ n, IsHS (K n)) (hK₀ : IsHS K₀)
    (hlim : Tendsto (fun n => hsNorm (K n - K₀)) atTop (nhds 0))
    (z : ℂ) :
    Tendsto (fun n => entireDet2 (K n) z) atTop (nhds (entireDet2 K₀ z))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  rcases eq_or_ne z 0 with rfl | hz
  · have hn : ∀ n, entireDet2 (K n) 0 = 1 := fun n =>
      (isRegularizedDet_entireDet2 (hK n)).eq_one_at_zero
    have h₀ : entireDet2 K₀ 0 = 1 :=
      (isRegularizedDet_entireDet2 hK₀).eq_one_at_zero
    simp_rw [hn, h₀]
    exact tendsto_const_nhds
  · set M : ℝ := hsNorm K₀ + 1 with hMdef
    have hbounded : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, hsNorm (K n) ≤ M := by
      have hsmall := hlim.eventually (eventually_lt_nhds (show (0 : ℝ) < 1 by norm_num))
      filter_upwards [hsmall] with n hn
      have hsplit : hsNorm (K n) ≤ hsNorm (K n - K₀) + hsNorm K₀ := by
        have heq : K n = (K n - K₀) + K₀ := by
          funext p
          simp
        calc
          hsNorm (K n) = hsNorm ((K n - K₀) + K₀) := congrArg hsNorm heq
          _ ≤ hsNorm (K n - K₀) + hsNorm K₀ :=
            hsNorm_add_le (isHS_sub (hK n) hK₀) hK₀
      rw [hMdef]
      linarith
    have hz0 : 0 < ‖z‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr hz
    set R : ℝ := 2 * ‖z‖ with hRdef
    have hR : 0 < R := by rw [hRdef]; positivity
    set E : ℝ := Real.exp (R ^ 2 * M ^ 2 / 2) with hEdef
    set bnd : ℕ → ℝ := fun k => E * (1 / 2) ^ k with hbnd
    have hsumbnd : Summable bnd := by
      rw [hbnd]
      exact (summable_geometric_of_lt_one (by norm_num) (by norm_num)).mul_left E
    have hterm_bound : ∀ (A : ι × ι → ℂ), IsHS A → hsNorm A ≤ M → ∀ k,
        ‖detCoeff A k * z ^ k‖ ≤ bnd k := by
      intro A hA hAM k
      have hAsq : hsNormSq A ≤ M ^ 2 := by
        have heq : hsNormSq A = hsNorm A ^ 2 := by
          rw [hsNorm, Real.sq_sqrt (hsNormSq_nonneg A)]
        rw [heq]
        exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (hsNorm_nonneg A) hAM 2
      have hcoeff : ‖detCoeff A k‖ ≤ E / R ^ k := by
        refine le_trans (norm_detCoeff_le hA hR k) ?_
        apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ (by positivity)
        rw [hEdef]
        exact Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by nlinarith [sq_nonneg R])
      rw [norm_mul, norm_pow, hbnd]
      have hzk : ‖z‖ ^ k ≠ 0 := by positivity
      have hkey : (E / R ^ k) * ‖z‖ ^ k = E * (1 / 2) ^ k := by
        have hRk : R ^ k = 2 ^ k * ‖z‖ ^ k := by rw [hRdef, mul_pow]
        rw [hRk, div_pow, one_pow]
        field_simp
      calc
        ‖detCoeff A k‖ * ‖z‖ ^ k ≤ (E / R ^ k) * ‖z‖ ^ k :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcoeff (by positivity)
        _ = E * (1 / 2) ^ k := hkey
    have hpoint : ∀ k : ℕ, Tendsto
        (fun n => detCoeff (K n) k * z ^ k) atTop
        (nhds (detCoeff K₀ k * z ^ k)) := by
      intro k
      exact (tendsto_detCoeff_of_hsNorm_sub_tendsto_zero K K₀ hK hK₀ hlim k).mul_const _
    have hdom : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ,
        ‖detCoeff (K n) k * z ^ k‖ ≤ bnd k := by
      filter_upwards [hbounded] with n hn
      exact hterm_bound (K n) (hK n) hn
    have hconv := tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence (𝓕 := (atTop : Filter ℕ))
      (f := fun n k => detCoeff (K n) k * z ^ k)
      (g := fun k => detCoeff K₀ k * z ^ k) hsumbnd hpoint hdom
    simpa only [entireDet2, entireOfCoeffs] using hconv

/-- **Operator-valued firewall.** A determinant zero at one fixed normalized spectral coordinate
cannot persist along Hilbert--Schmidt kernels converging to a base kernel whose determinant is
nonzero at that coordinate. -/

source_arguments.statement:
theorem tendsto_boundary_centeredSchur_energy :
    Tendsto (fun ω : ℝ => ∫ τ : ℝ, ‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
        centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2)
      (nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds 0)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendsto_boundary_centeredSchur_energy :
    Tendsto (fun ω : ℝ => ∫ τ : ℝ, ‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
        centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2)
      (nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds 0)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨ω₀, K, lam, hω₀, hK, hlam, hbound⟩ := exists_uniform_centered_bound
  have hev : ∀ᶠ ω : ℝ in nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0), 0 < ω ∧ ω ≤ ω₀ := by
    filter_upwards [Ioc_mem_nhdsGT hω₀] with ω hω
    exact ⟨hω.1, hω.2⟩
  have hlimfun : ∀ τ : ℝ, τ ≠ 0 →
      ‖centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ lam * boundaryMajorant K τ := by
    intro τ hτ
    have hz0 : ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 := by
      simp only [ne_eq, mul_eq_zero, Complex.I_ne_zero, or_false, Complex.ofReal_eq_zero]
      exact hτ
    have hzre : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I).re := by simp
    have hlim := (tendsto_centeredSchurQuotient hzre hz0).norm
    refine le_of_tendsto hlim ?_
    filter_upwards [hev] with ω hω
    exact hbound ω hω.1 hω.2 τ hτ
  have hcontlim : ContinuousOn (fun τ : ℝ => centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I))
      {t : ℝ | t ≠ 0} := by
    intro τ hτ0
    have hτ : τ ≠ 0 := hτ0
    have hz0 : ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 := by
      simp only [ne_eq, mul_eq_zero, Complex.I_ne_zero, or_false, Complex.ofReal_eq_zero]
      exact hτ
    have hne1 : (1 : ℂ) + (τ : ℂ) * Complex.I ≠ 1 := line_ne_one (by simp) hτ
    have hζ0 : riemannZeta ((1 : ℂ) + (τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 := by
      refine riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re ?_
      simp
    have hz : ContinuousAt (fun t : ℝ => ((t : ℂ) * Complex.I)) τ := by
      have : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => ((t : ℂ) * Complex.I)) := by continuity
      exact this.continuousAt
    have hA : ContinuousAt (fun t : ℝ => riemannZeta (1 + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I)) τ :=
      continuousAt_zeta_line hne1
    have hcont : ContinuousAt
        (fun t : ℝ => centeredSchurLimit ((t : ℂ) * Complex.I)) τ := by
      refine continuousAt_const.div (hz.mul hA) ?_
      exact mul_ne_zero hz0 hζ0
    exact hcont.continuousWithinAt
  have hmeas : ∀ᶠ ω : ℝ in nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0),
      AEStronglyMeasurable (fun τ : ℝ =>
        ‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
          centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2) volume := by
    filter_upwards [hev] with ω hω
    have h1 := aestronglyMeasurable_of_continuousOn_ne_zero
      (continuousOn_centeredSchurQuotient_line hω.1)
    have h2 := aestronglyMeasurable_of_continuousOn_ne_zero hcontlim
    exact ((h1.sub h2).norm.pow 2)
  have hdom : ∀ᶠ ω : ℝ in nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0), ∀ᵐ τ : ℝ,
      ‖‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
        centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2‖ ≤ lam ^ 2 * boundaryBound K τ := by
    filter_upwards [hev] with ω hω
    filter_upwards [compl_mem_ae_iff.2 Real.volume_singleton] with τ hτmem
    have hτ : τ ≠ 0 := hτmem
    have h1 := hbound ω hω.1 hω.2 τ hτ
    have h2 := hlimfun τ hτ
    have h3 : ‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
        centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ 2 * (lam * boundaryMajorant K τ) := by
      refine le_trans (norm_sub_le _ _) ?_
      linarith
    have h4 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
        centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ := norm_nonneg _
    have hmaj : (0 : ℝ) ≤ boundaryMajorant K τ := boundaryMajorant_nonneg hK τ
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (by positivity), boundaryBound_eq K τ]
    calc ‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
          centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2
        ≤ (2 * (lam * boundaryMajorant K τ)) ^ 2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ h4 h3 2
      _ = lam ^ 2 * (4 * boundaryMajorant K τ ^ 2) := by ring
  have hlim : ∀ᵐ τ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun ω : ℝ =>
      ‖centeredSchurQuotient ω ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) -
        centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2)
      (nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds 0) := by
    filter_upwards [compl_mem_ae_iff.2 Real.volume_singleton] with τ hτmem
    have hτ : τ ≠ 0 := hτmem
    have hz0 : ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 := by
      simp only [ne_eq, mul_eq_zero, Complex.I_ne_zero, or_false, Complex.ofReal_eq_zero]
      exact hτ
    have hzre : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I).re := by simp
    have hpt := tendsto_centeredSchurQuotient hzre hz0
    have h := ((hpt.sub (tendsto_const_nhds
      (x := centeredSchurLimit ((τ : ℂ) * Complex.I)))).norm.pow 2)
    simpa using h
  have hDCT := tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence
    (fun τ : ℝ => lam ^ 2 * boundaryBound K τ) hmeas hdom
    ((integrable_boundaryBound K).const_mul (lam ^ 2)) hlim
  simpa using hDCT

method.description: Establishes pointwise convergence and domination to apply dominated convergence theorem
evidence: obtain ⟨ω₀, K, lam, hω₀, hK, hlam, hbound⟩ := exists_uniform_centered_bound
have hmeas : ∀ᶠ ω : ℝ in nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0),
(fun τ : ℝ => lam ^ 2 * boundaryBound K τ) hmeas hdom

source_arguments.statement:
theorem tendsto_coprimeRemainder_factorial {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) (hs1 : s ≠ 1) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => coprimeRemainder s N.factorial) atTop
      (𝓝 (normalizedWeightedRemainder s 1))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendsto_coprimeRemainder_factorial {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) (hs1 : s ≠ 1) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => coprimeRemainder s N.factorial) atTop
      (𝓝 (normalizedWeightedRemainder s 1))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  classical
  let g : ℕ+ → ℂ := fun n => if n = 1 then normalizedWeightedRemainder s n else 0
  have hl : ∀ n : ℕ+, Tendsto
      (fun N : ℕ => if N.factorial.Coprime (n : ℕ) then normalizedWeightedRemainder s n else 0)
      atTop (𝓝 (g n)) := by
    intro n
    apply tendsto_const_nhds.congr'
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (n : ℕ)] with N hN
    by_cases hn : n = 1
    · simp [hn, g]
    · have hn1 : (n : ℕ) ≠ 1 := by intro h; apply hn; exact PNat.eq h
      have hc : ¬ N.factorial.Coprime (n : ℕ) := by
        intro hc
        have := coprime_factorial_forces_large n.pos (dvd_refl _) hc hn1
        omega
      simp [g, hn, hc]
  have hb : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ n : ℕ+,
      ‖if N.factorial.Coprime (n : ℕ) then normalizedWeightedRemainder s n else 0‖
      ≤ ‖normalizedWeightedRemainder s n‖ := by
    filter_upwards [] with N n
    split_ifs <;> simp
  have h := tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence
    (summable_normalizedWeighted hs hs1).norm hl hb
  simpa only [g, tsum_ite_eq, PNat.val_ofNat, coprimeRemainder] using h

method.description: Proves tendsto of coprimeRemainder using dominated convergence and summability of normalizedWeightedRemainder
steps: show dominated convergence via hl and hb

theorem tendsto_routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallFredholmEntireDet_nhdsGT_zero (z : ℂ) :

        (routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallHalfLineLaw d) z)
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))

theorem tendsto_routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallFredholmEntireDet_nhdsGT_zero (z : ℂ) :

        (routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallHalfLineLaw d) z)
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))
      (𝓝 (routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallFredholmEntireDet (expMeasure 1) z))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  unfold routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallFredholmEntireDet
  apply tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence
    (ContinuousKernelFredholm.summable_hadamard_majorant ‖z‖ (norm_nonneg z))
  · intro n
    exact tendsto_const_nhds.mul
      (tendsto_routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallFredholmCoefficient_nhdsGT_zero n)
  · exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun d n => by
      rw [norm_mul, norm_pow]
      calc
        ‖z‖ ^ n * ‖routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallFredholmCoefficient
            (routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallHalfLineLaw d) n‖ ≤
            ‖z‖ ^ n * ((Real.sqrt n) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)) := by
          gcongr
          exact norm_routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallFredholmCoefficient_le
            (routePPrimitiveGammaJuliaStokesWallHalfLineLaw d)
            (wallHalfLineLaw_Iio_zero d) n
        _ = (Real.sqrt n * ‖z‖) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ) := by ring

by
  classical
  rw [← tsum_near_pole_bound hc]
  have hsumeq : ∀ n : ℕ, (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (count n), (1/(n:ℝ)^2)*(rcsch (dist n k /2))^2)
      = ∑' k : ℕ, (if k < count n then (1/(n:ℝ)^2)*(rcsch (dist n k /2))^2 else 0) := by
    intro n
    rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := Finset.range (count n))
      (fun k hk => by rw [Finset.mem_range] at hk; simp [hk])]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k hk => by rw [Finset.mem_range] at hk; simp [hk])
  simp_rw [hsumeq]
  apply tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence (summable_near_pole_bound hc)
  · intro k
    have hev : (fun n : ℕ => (1/(n:ℝ)^2)*(rcsch (dist n k /2))^2)
        =ᶠ[atTop] (fun n => if k < count n then (1/(n:ℝ)^2)*(rcsch (dist n k /2))^2 else 0) := by
      filter_upwards [hcount.eventually_gt_atTop k] with n hn; simp [hn]
    exact (tendsto_rescaled_csch_sq_term (show (0:ℝ) < c*((k:ℝ)+1/2) by positivity)
      (hpos k) (hlim k)).congr' hev
  · filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop 0] with n hn k
    by_cases hkc : k < count n
    · rw [if_pos hkc, Real.norm_of_nonneg (by positivity)]
      have hdpos : 0 < dist n k := lt_of_lt_of_le (by positivity) (hlb n k hn hkc)
      exact rescaled_csch_sq_le hc k hn hdpos (hlb n k hn hkc)
    · rw [if_neg hkc, norm_zero]; positivity

# Reflected bi-heat measure-separated sign rate cone

- **ID:** RBH-MSSF
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** CONTINUUM INCOMMENSURATE SIGNED RECEIVER CLASSIFICATION
- **Parent:** RBH-CSSF
- **Frontier-map policy:** read only

## Frozen conjecture

Let `P,Q` be nonzero finite positive Borel measures on rate space.  For one
`kappa>0`, assume

- `0<r<kappa` for `P`-almost every rate;
- `kappa≤r` for `Q`-almost every rate;
- `∫ sinh(r*T) dQ < ∞` for every `T>0`.

Define continuum reporter and wall derivative

`F(t) = -∫ sinh(r*t) dP(r) + ∫ sinh(r*t) dQ(r)`,

`D = ∫ r dQ(r) - ∫ r dP(r)`.

Prove exact classifications

`0≤D ↔ ∀t>0, 0<F(t)`

and

`0≤D ↔ ∀t, F(t)=0 ↔ t=0`.

Then factor arbitrary real-power RBH aperture integrals and derive an exact RH
receiver for every measure packet in cone.

## Corpus basis

- RBH-CSSF proves countable theorem by dominated `tsum`, strict separator
  comparison, low-tail normalization, and local uniform convergence.
- `measure_eq_of_laplace_eq` and continuum spectral-measure modules supply
  finite-measure and Laplace-transform infrastructure.
- Mandatory corpus search found no separated-support hyperbolic-sine integral
  cone.

## Attack

1. Derive low and first-moment integrability from finite mass and bounded support;
   derive high first-moment integrability from positive hyperbolic moment at `T=1`.
2. Apply dominated convergence to `F(t)/t` as `t→0+`.
3. Integrate separator comparison for `sinh(r*t)/r`; strictness follows from
   positive low mass and an almost-everywhere strict integrand.
4. Normalize low integral by `sinh(kappa*t)`.  Pointwise decay plus unit
   domination gives zero by dominated convergence; positive high mass supplies
   eventual lower bound `Q(univ)*sinh(kappa*t)`.
5. Endpoint domination gives compact-interval continuity; IVT converts `D<0`
   into additional positive zero.
6. Transport through continuum real-power aperture factorization.

## Provisional literature audit

Variation-diminishing Laplace-transform theory is classical.  The primary
source checked (Grussler--Sepulchre, arXiv:2006.10030) treats finite-dimensional
Toeplitz/Hankel systems and does not state this continuum hyperbolic-sine
moment-cone classification or RBH aperture theorem.  Search found applications
invoking general variation diminution, but no exact match.  Priority remains
provisional pending expert review.

## New exact insight

Atomicity and countability are irrelevant to separated-sign RBH rigidity.
Arbitrary nonzero finite positive Borel rate measures obey same exact cone, with
no uniform distance between low support and separator.  First wall moment is
complete invariant for zero exclusion.

At infinity, entire low measure becomes negligible after normalization by
`sinh(kappa*t)` through dominated convergence.  Positive high mass—not a high
atom—then forces eventual positivity.  Thus accumulation and continuous rate
spectra create no hidden cancellation chamber.

Continuum real-power aperture integration transports classification to exact RH
receivers.

## Failure boundaries

- Signed measures with more than one support-order sign change.
- Positive mass on separator from low side (`r=kappa`).
- Infinite measures or missing high hyperbolic moments.
- Source-derived measure law and non-diagonal rate collisions.

# CFI critical-boundary singular cancellation

- **ID:** CFI-CBSC
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean)
- **Source:** `rh-current-frontier-map.md` · CFI / CCM-FU critical incidence
- **Statement:** For every `0 < ω < 1/2`, the full normalized CFI coupled error has a square-integrable boundary value at `δ = 0`, and its `δ > 0` regularizations converge to that boundary strongly in `L²(0,∞)`.

## Goal

Discharge CFI's critical `LAND` premise without assuming RH.  The exact proof chain is:

```text
critical lower-minus-upper singular cancellation
  → closed CFI boundary carrier at δ = 0
  → existing pre-scalar affine boundary-renormalization/source-response identity
  → CFI / CCM-FU no longer owes construction of the singular boundary carrier
  → remaining burden is the existing graph-debt/source-order scalar
  → four-unit endpoint
  → RH.
```

This theorem does not assert the graph-debt/source-order scalar and therefore is not a disguised RH
assumption.  It removes the analytic carrier premise on which that final scalar is meant to act.

## Gates

- [x] 0 → 1  in-progress: well-posed, source-pure, attack idea, Door passport sketch
- [x] 1 → 2  fully-proven: complete paper proof, `[PROVED HERE]`, no open dependency
- [x] 2 → 3  formalized: Lean theorem, targeted `lake build` green, axiom audit PASS
- [ ] 3 → 4  publication-ready: standalone paper (theorem + proof + Lean certificate + Door-2)

## Conjecture

Write

```text
F_{ω,δ}(t) = exp(-(1+ω+δ)t) E_ω(exp t).
```

For every `ω ∈ (0,1/2)`:

1. `t ↦ F_{ω,0}(t)^2` is integrable on `(0,∞)`;
2. as `δ → 0` through `δ ≥ 0`,
   `∫₀∞ (F_{ω,δ}(t)-F_{ω,0}(t))² dt → 0`.

The final Lean capstone must quantify over `ω`; it will have no ambient premise, added axiom, or
unclosed hypothesis.

## Corpus basis and novelty audit

- `CoupledFloorMobiusShiftIncidence.lean` gives exact lower-minus-upper incidence and proves the
  common upper input `q_δ` has squared norm `1/(2δ)`, hence is not itself in `L²` at `δ = 0`.
- `ShiftedEulerFloorMobiusTailCoupling.lean` proves the natural-argument envelope
  `|E_ω(N)| ≤ C_ω N^(1-ω)`.
- `SuzukiTailSummatoryErrorTransform.lean` defines the real-argument error through `⌊X⌋₊`.
- Corpus searches for `coupledErrorVector critical boundary L2 singular cancellation damping
  convergence` found no critical combined-vector integrability or strong-boundary theorem.
- Literature searches through August 2026 found work on Möbius summatory distributions,
  Möbius/screw functions, and scaling-Hamiltonian RH criteria, but no theorem identifying this exact
  shifted-Euler lower-minus-upper incidence as an `L²` critical boundary value.  Novelty claim is
  confined to this exact carrier theorem and proof-chain use.

## Approach

1. Upgrade the corpus natural-argument envelope to real `X ≥ 1`.  With `N = ⌊X⌋₊`, split
   `E_ω(X) = E_ω(N) + M_ω(N)-M_ω(X)`.  The first term is in the corpus; a mean-value/rpow estimate
   bounds the one-cell main-term jump by `O(X^ω)`, hence by `O(X^(1-ω))` because `ω < 1/2`.
2. Substitute `X = exp t`: `|F_{ω,0}(t)| ≤ C exp(-2ωt)`.  Its square is dominated by an integrable
   exponential.
3. Prove the exact damping identity `F_{ω,δ}(t) = exp(-δt) F_{ω,0}(t)`.
4. For `δ ≥ 0`, the squared difference is dominated by `F_{ω,0}(t)^2` and converges pointwise to
   zero.  Dominated convergence gives strong `L²` convergence.

## Proof

**[PROVED HERE]** Fix `0 < ω < 1/2`.  The corpus theorem
`abs_suzukiCoupledError_le` supplies `C > 0` with

```text
|E_ω(N)| ≤ C N^(1-ω)                    (N ≥ 1).
```

For real `X ≥ 1`, put `N = ⌊X⌋₊`.  The summatory part is constant on the floor cell, so

```text
E_ω(X) = E_ω(N) + M_ω(N) - M_ω(X).
```

Here `N ≤ X < N+1`.  The corpus rpow Lipschitz theorem
`abs_rpow_sub_rpow_le_of_le`, applied with exponent `1+ω`, gives

```text
|N^(1+ω)-X^(1+ω)| ≤ (1+ω) X^ω |N-X| ≤ (1+ω) X^ω.
```

After multiplication by the main-term density and division by `1+ω`, the floor-cell correction is
at most `|r_ω|X^ω`.  Since `X ≥ 1` and `ω < 1/2`, `X^ω ≤ X^(1-ω)`.  Thus some `C' > 0` satisfies
`|E_ω(X)| ≤ C'X^(1-ω)` for every real `X ≥ 1`.

For `t ≥ 0`, substitute `X = exp t`:

```text
|F_{ω,0}(t)|
  = exp(-(1+ω)t) |E_ω(exp t)|
  ≤ C' exp(-2ωt).
```

Consequently `F_{ω,0}²` is dominated by `C'² exp(-4ωt)`, which is integrable on `(0,∞)`.
Directly from the definition,

```text
F_{ω,δ}(t) = exp(-δt) F_{ω,0}(t).
```

For `δ,t ≥ 0`, `|exp(-δt)-1| ≤ 1`; hence

```text
|F_{ω,δ}(t)-F_{ω,0}(t)|² ≤ |F_{ω,0}(t)|².
```

The left side tends pointwise to zero as `δ → 0` within `[0,∞)`.  Dominated convergence proves its
integral tends to zero, exactly strong `L²` convergence.  The existing incidence theorem identifies
`F_{ω,0}` pointwise with the full lower-minus-upper `tsum`, while the existing damping-mode theorem
shows the uncancelled upper input's squared norm tends to infinity.  This completes the claimed
singular-cancellation certificate with no open dependency.

# The dominated convergence theorem

This file collects various results related to the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem
for the Bochner integral.

## Main results

  the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for the Bochner integral
- `MeasureTheory.hasSum_integral_of_dominated_convergence`:
  the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for series
- `MeasureTheory.integral_tsum`, `MeasureTheory.integral_tsum_of_summable_integral_norm`:
  the integral and `tsum`s commute, if the norms of the functions form a summable series
- `intervalIntegral.hasSum_integral_of_dominated_convergence`: the Lebesgue dominated convergence
  theorem for parametric interval integrals
