/-!
## The Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for the Bochner integral
-/
section DominatedConvergenceTheorem

open Set Filter TopologicalSpace ENNReal
open scoped Topology Interval

namespace MeasureTheory

variable {α E G : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G]
  {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α}

/-- **Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem** provides sufficient conditions under which almost
  everywhere convergence of a sequence of functions implies the convergence of their integrals.
  We could weaken the condition `bound_integrable` to require `HasFiniteIntegral bound μ` instead
  (i.e. not requiring that `bound` is measurable), but in all applications proving integrability
  is easier. -/
theorem tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence {F : ℕ → α → G} {f : α → G} (bound : α → ℝ)
    (F_measurable : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) μ) (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ)
    (h_bound : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖F n a‖ ≤ bound a)
    (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => F n a) atTop (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ a, F n a ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 <| ∫ a, f a ∂μ) := by
  simp only [integral_eq_setToFun]
  exact tendsto_setToFun_of_dominated_convergence (dominatedFinMeasAdditive_weightedSMul μ)
    bound F_measurable bound_integrable h_bound h_lim

/-- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for filters with a countable basis -/
theorem tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence {ι} {l : Filter ι} [l.IsCountablyGenerated]
    {F : ι → α → G} {f : α → G} (bound : α → ℝ) (hF_meas : ∀ᶠ n in l, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) μ)
    (h_bound : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖F n a‖ ≤ bound a) (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ)
    (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => F n a) l (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ a, F n a ∂μ) l (𝓝 <| ∫ a, f a ∂μ) := by
  simp only [integral_eq_setToFun]
  exact tendsto_setToFun_filter_of_dominated_convergence (dominatedFinMeasAdditive_weightedSMul μ)
    bound hF_meas h_bound bound_integrable h_lim

/-- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for series. -/
theorem hasSum_integral_of_dominated_convergence {ι} [Countable ι] {F : ι → α → G} {f : α → G}
    (bound : ι → α → ℝ) (hF_meas : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) μ)
    (h_bound : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖F n a‖ ≤ bound n a)
    (bound_summable : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Summable fun n => bound n a)
    (bound_integrable : Integrable (fun a => ∑' n, bound n a) μ)
    (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, HasSum (fun n => F n a) (f a)) :
    HasSum (fun n => ∫ a, F n a ∂μ) (∫ a, f a ∂μ) := by
  simp only [integral_eq_setToFun]
  exact hasSum_setToFun_of_dominated_convergence _ bound hF_meas h_bound bound_summable
    bound_integrable h_lim

theorem integral_tsum {ι} [Countable ι] {f : ι → α → G} (hf : ∀ i, AEStronglyMeasurable (f i) μ)
    (hf' : ∑' i, ∫⁻ a : α, ‖f i a‖ₑ ∂μ ≠ ∞) :
    ∫ a, ∑' i, f i a ∂μ = ∑' i, ∫ a, f i a ∂μ := by
  by_cases hG : CompleteSpace G; swap
  · simp [integral, hG]
  simp only [integral_eq_setToFun]
  exact setToFun_tsum _ hf hf'

lemma hasSum_integral_of_summable_integral_norm {ι} [Countable ι] {F : ι → α → E}
    (hF_int : ∀ i : ι, Integrable (F i) μ) (hF_sum : Summable fun i ↦ ∫ a, ‖F i a‖ ∂μ) :
    HasSum (∫ a, F · a ∂μ) (∫ a, (∑' i, F i a) ∂μ) := by
  by_cases hE : CompleteSpace E; swap
  · simp [integral, hE, hasSum_zero]
  rw [integral_tsum (fun i ↦ (hF_int i).1)]
  · exact (hF_sum.of_norm_bounded fun i ↦ norm_integral_le_integral_norm _).hasSum
  have (i : ι) : ∫⁻ a, ‖F i a‖ₑ ∂μ = ‖∫ a, ‖F i a‖ ∂μ‖ₑ := by
    dsimp [enorm]
    rw [lintegral_coe_eq_integral _ (hF_int i).norm, coe_nnreal_eq, coe_nnnorm,

_bound : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, ‖F n a‖ ≤ bound a)
    (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, Tendsto (fun n ↦ F n a) atTop (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫ᵛ a, F n a ∂[B; μ]) atTop (𝓝 <| ∫ᵛ a, f a ∂[B; μ]) :=
  tendsto_setToFun_of_dominated_convergence _ bound F_measurable bound_integrable h_bound h_lim

/-- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for filters with a countable basis -/
theorem tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence {l : Filter ι} [l.IsCountablyGenerated]
    {F : ι → X → E} {f : X → E} (bound : X → ℝ)
    (hF_meas : ∀ᶠ n in l, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) μ.variation)
    (h_bound : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, ‖F n a‖ ≤ bound a)
    (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ.variation)
    (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, Tendsto (fun n ↦ F n a) l (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫ᵛ a, F n a ∂[B; μ]) l (𝓝 <| ∫ᵛ a, f a ∂[B; μ]) :=
  tendsto_setToFun_filter_of_dominated_convergence _ bound hF_meas h_bound bound_integrable h_lim

/-- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for series. -/
theorem hasSum_integral_of_dominated_convergence [Countable ι] {F : ι → X → E} {f : X → E}
    (bound : ι → X → ℝ) (hF_meas : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) μ.variation)
    (h_bound : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, ‖F n a‖ ≤ bound n a)
    (bound_summable : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, Summable fun n ↦ bound n a)
    (bound_integrable : Integrable (fun a ↦ ∑' n, bound n a) μ.variation)
    (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, HasSum (fun n ↦ F n a) (f a)) :
    HasSum (fun n ↦ ∫ᵛ a, F n a ∂[B; μ]) (∫ᵛ a, f a ∂[B; μ]) :=
  hasSum_setToFun_of_dominated_convergence _ bound hF_meas h_bound bound_summable bound_integrable
    h_lim

theorem integral_tsum [CompleteSpace E] [Countable ι]
    {f : ι → X → E} (hf : ∀ i, AEStronglyMeasurable (f i) μ.variation)
    (hf' : ∑' i, ∫⁻ a : X, ‖f i a‖ₑ ∂μ.variation ≠ ∞) :
    ∫ᵛ a, ∑' i, f i a ∂[B; μ] = ∑' i, ∫ᵛ a, f i a ∂[B; μ] :=
  setToFun_tsum _ hf hf'

/-- Corollary of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem: If a sequence of functions `F n` is
(eventually) uniformly bounded by a constant and converges (eventually) pointwise to a
function `f`, then the integrals of `F n` with respect to a vector measure `μ` with finite
variation converge to the integral of `f`. -/
theorem tendsto_integral_filter_of_norm_le_const {l : Filter ι} [l.IsCountablyGenerated]
    {F : ι → X → E} [IsFiniteMeasure μ.variation] {f : X → E}
    (h_meas : ∀ᶠ n in l, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) μ.variation)
    (h_bound : ∃ C, ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, ‖F n a‖ ≤ C)
    (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ.variation, Tendsto (fun n ↦ F n a) l (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫ᵛ a, F n a ∂[B; μ]) l (𝓝 (∫ᵛ a, f a ∂[B; μ])) :=
  tendsto_setToFun_filter_of_norm_le_const _ h_meas h_bound h_lim

end VectorMeasure

end MeasureTheory

/-!
# Dominated convergence theorem

Lebesgue's dominated convergence theorem states that the limit and Lebesgue integral of
a sequence of (almost everywhere) measurable functions can be swapped if the functions are
pointwise dominated by a fixed function. This file provides a few variants of the result.
-/

public section

open Filter ENNReal Topology

namespace MeasureTheory

variable {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {μ : Measure α}

theorem limsup_lintegral_le {f : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞} (g : α → ℝ≥0∞) (hf_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (f n))
    (h_bound : ∀ n, f n ≤ᵐ[μ] g) (h_fin : ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ ≠ ∞) :
    limsup (fun n => ∫⁻ a, f n a ∂μ) atTop ≤ ∫⁻ a, limsup (fun n => f n a) atTop ∂μ :=
  calc
    limsup (fun n => ∫⁻ a, f n a ∂μ) atTop = ⨅ n : ℕ, ⨆ i ≥ n, ∫⁻ a, f i a ∂μ :=
      limsup_eq_iInf_iSup_of_nat
    _ ≤ ⨅ n : ℕ, ∫⁻ a, ⨆ i ≥ n, f i a ∂μ := iInf_mono fun _ => iSup₂_lintegral_le _
    _ = ∫⁻ a, ⨅ n : ℕ, ⨆ i ≥ n, f i a ∂μ := by
      refine (lintegral_iInf ?_ ?_ ?_).symm
      · intro n
        exact .biSup _ (Set.to_countable _) (fun i _ ↦ hf_meas i)
      · intro n m hnm a
        exact iSup_le_iSup_of_subset fun i hi => le_trans hnm hi
      · refine ne_top_of_le_ne_top h_fin (lintegral_mono_ae ?_)
        refine (ae_all_iff.2 h_bound).mono fun n hn => ?_
        exact iSup_le fun i => iSup_le fun _ => hn i
    _ = ∫⁻ a, limsup (fun n => f n a) atTop ∂μ := by simp only [limsup_eq_iInf_iSup_of_nat]

/-- **Dominated convergence theorem** for nonnegative `Measurable` functions. -/
theorem tendsto_lintegral_of_dominated_convergence {F : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞}
    (bound : α → ℝ≥0∞) (hF_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (F n)) (h_bound : ∀ n, F n ≤ᵐ[μ] bound)
    (h_fin : ∫⁻ a, bound a ∂μ ≠ ∞) (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => F n a) atTop (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫⁻ a, F n a ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ)) :=
  tendsto_of_le_liminf_of_limsup_le
    (calc
      ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, liminf (fun n : ℕ => F n a) atTop ∂μ :=
        lintegral_congr_ae <| h_lim.mono fun _ h => h.liminf_eq.symm
      _ ≤ liminf (fun n => ∫⁻ a, F n a ∂μ) atTop := lintegral_liminf_le hF_meas)
    (calc
      limsup (fun n : ℕ => ∫⁻ a, F n a ∂μ) atTop ≤ ∫⁻ a, limsup (fun n => F n a) atTop ∂μ :=
        limsup_lintegral_le _ hF_meas h_bound h_fin
      _ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ := lintegral_congr_ae <| h_lim.mono fun _ h => h.limsup_eq)

/-- **Dominated convergence theorem** for nonnegative `AEMeasurable` functions. -/
theorem tendsto_lintegral_of_dominated_convergence' {F : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞}
    (bound : α → ℝ≥0∞) (hF_meas : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (F n) μ) (h_bound : ∀ n, F n ≤ᵐ[μ] bound)
    (h_fin : ∫⁻ a, bound a ∂μ ≠ ∞) (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => F n a) atTop (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫⁻ a, F n a ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ)) := by
  have : ∀ n, ∫⁻ a, F n a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, (hF_meas n).mk (F n) a ∂μ := fun n =>
    lintegral_congr_ae (hF_meas n).ae_eq_mk
  simp_rw [this]
  apply
    tendsto_lintegral_of_dominated_convergence bound (fun n => (hF_meas n).measurable_mk) _ h_fin
  · have : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, (hF_meas n).mk (F n) a = F n a := fun n => (hF_meas n).ae_eq_mk.symm
    have : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ∀ n, (hF_meas n).mk (F n) a = F n a := ae_all_iff.mpr this
    filter_upwards [this, h_lim] with a H H'
    simp_rw [H]
    exact H'
  · intro n
    filter_upwards [h_bound n, (hF_meas n).ae_eq_mk] with a H H'
    rwa [H'] at H

/-- **Dominated convergence theorem** for filters with a countable basis and
AEMeasurable functions. -/
theorem tendsto_lintegral_filter_of_dominated_convergence' {ι} {l : Filter ι}
    [l.IsCountablyGenerated] {F : ι → α → ℝ≥0∞} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (bound : α → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hF_meas : ∀ᶠ n in l, AEMeasurable (F n) μ) (h_bound : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, F n a ≤ bound a)
    (h_fin : ∫⁻ a, bound a ∂μ ≠ ∞) (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => F n a) l (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫⁻ a, F n a ∂μ) l (𝓝 <| ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ) := by
  rw [tendsto_iff_seq_tendsto]
  intro x xl
  have hxl := by
    rw [tendsto_atTop'] at xl
    exact xl
  have h := inter_mem hF_meas h_bound
  replace h := hxl _ h
  rcases h with ⟨k, h⟩
  rw [← tendsto_add_atTop_iff_nat k]
  refine tendsto_lintegral_of_dominated_convergence' ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · exact bound
  · intro
    refine (h _ ?_).1
    exact Nat.le_add_left _ _
  · intro
    refine (h _ ?_).2
    exact Nat.le_add_left _ _
  · assumption
  · refine h_lim.mono fun a h_lim => ?_
    apply @Tendsto.comp _ _ _ (fun n => x (n + k)) fun n => F n a
    · assumption
    rw [tendsto_add_atTop_iff_nat]
    assumption

/-- **Dominated convergence theorem** for filters with a countable basis. -/
theorem tendsto_lintegral_filter_of_dominated_convergence {ι} {l : Filter ι}

/-!
# Infinite products in normed rings

This file proves a dominated convergence theorem for infinite products of terms of the form
`(1 + f n k)` in a complete normed commutative ring, by reducing to the additive version
(Tannery's theorem) via the formal expansion `∏ (1 + f i) = ∑ₛ ∏ᵢ∈ₛ f i`.

## Main results

* `tendsto_tprod_one_add_of_dominated_convergence`: if `f n k → g k` pointwise and
  `‖f n k‖ ≤ bound k` eventually with `bound` summable, then
  `∏' k, (1 + f n k) → ∏' k, (1 + g k)`.
-/

open Topology Filter

variable {α R β : Type*} [NormedCommRing R] [NormOneClass R] [CompleteSpace R] {g : β → R}
  {bound : β → ℝ}

/-- Dominated convergence for infinite products: if `f n k → g k` for all `k` and
`‖f n k‖ ≤ bound k` eventually with `bound` summable,
then `∏' k, (1 + f n k) → ∏' k, (1 + g k)`. -/
public theorem tendsto_tprod_one_add_of_dominated_convergence {𝓕 : Filter α} {f : α → β → R}
    (h_sum : Summable bound) (hab : ∀ k, Tendsto (f · k) 𝓕 (𝓝 (g k)))
    (h_bound : ∀ᶠ n in 𝓕, ∀ k, ‖f n k‖ ≤ bound k) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∏' k, (1 + f n k)) 𝓕 (𝓝 (∏' k, (1 + g k))) := by
  rcases eq_or_neBot 𝓕 with rfl | _
  · simp
  have h_bound_g (k) : ‖g k‖ ≤ bound k :=
    le_of_tendsto ((hab k).norm) (h_bound.mono fun n hn ↦ hn k)
  have hsum_g : Summable (‖g ·‖) := h_sum.of_nonneg_of_le (fun _ ↦ norm_nonneg _) h_bound_g
  rw [show ∏' k, (1 + g k) = ∑' s, ∏ i ∈ s, g i from
    tprod_one_add (summable_finsetProd_of_summable_norm hsum_g)]
  have : Tendsto (∑' k, ∏ c ∈ k, f · c) 𝓕 (𝓝 (∑' k, ∏ c ∈ k, g c)) :=
    tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence (summable_finsetProd_of_summable_nonneg
      (fun i ↦ (norm_nonneg (g i)).trans (h_bound_g i)) h_sum)
      (tendsto_finsetProd · fun i _ ↦ hab i)
      (h_bound.mono fun n hn s ↦ (Finset.norm_prod_le s (f n)).trans
      (Finset.prod_le_prod (by grind) (by grind)))
  apply this.congr' (h_bound.mono fun n hn ↦ ?_)
  rw [tprod_one_add]
  exact summable_finsetProd_of_summable_norm <| h_sum.of_nonneg_of_le (by grind) hn

simp_rw [s', SimpleFunc.coe_comp]; exact SimpleFunc.norm_approxOn_zero_le _ _ (x, y) n
      simp only [mem_setOf_eq, hfx, indicator_of_mem, this,
        ← setToFun_simpleFunc_eq_setToSimpleFunc hT, f']
      refine
        tendsto_setToFun_of_dominated_convergence hT (fun y => ‖f x y‖ + ‖f x y‖)
          (fun n => (s' n x).aestronglyMeasurable) (hfx.norm.add hfx.norm) ?_ ?_
      · refine fun n => Eventually.of_forall fun y =>
          SimpleFunc.norm_approxOn_zero_le ?_ ?_ (x, y) n
        · exact hf.measurable
        · simp
      · refine Eventually.of_forall fun y => SimpleFunc.tendsto_approxOn ?_ ?_ ?_
        · exact hf.measurable.of_uncurry_left
        · simp
        apply subset_closure
        simp [-Function.uncurry_apply_pair]
    · simp [f', hfx, setToFun_undef]
  exact stronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto _ hf' h2f'

variable {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [FirstCountableTopology X]

theorem continuousWithinAt_setToFun_of_dominated (hT : DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ T C)
    {fs : X → α → E} {x₀ : X} {bound : α → ℝ} {s : Set X}
    (hfs_meas : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] x₀, AEStronglyMeasurable (fs x) μ)
    (h_bound : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] x₀, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖fs x a‖ ≤ bound a) (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ)
    (h_cont : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ContinuousWithinAt (fun x => fs x a) s x₀) :
    ContinuousWithinAt (fun x => setToFun μ T hT (fs x)) s x₀ :=
  tendsto_setToFun_filter_of_dominated_convergence hT bound ‹_› ‹_› ‹_› ‹_›

theorem continuousAt_setToFun_of_dominated (hT : DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ T C) {fs : X → α → E}
    {x₀ : X} {bound : α → ℝ} (hfs_meas : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, AEStronglyMeasurable (fs x) μ)
    (h_bound : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖fs x a‖ ≤ bound a) (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ)
    (h_cont : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ContinuousAt (fun x => fs x a) x₀) :
    ContinuousAt (fun x => setToFun μ T hT (fs x)) x₀ :=
  tendsto_setToFun_filter_of_dominated_convergence hT bound ‹_› ‹_› ‹_› ‹_›

theorem continuousOn_setToFun_of_dominated (hT : DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ T C) {fs : X → α → E}
    {bound : α → ℝ} {s : Set X} (hfs_meas : ∀ x ∈ s, AEStronglyMeasurable (fs x) μ)
    (h_bound : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖fs x a‖ ≤ bound a) (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ)
    (h_cont : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun x => fs x a) s) :
    ContinuousOn (fun x => setToFun μ T hT (fs x)) s := by
  intro x hx
  refine continuousWithinAt_setToFun_of_dominated hT ?_ ?_ bound_integrable ?_
  · filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with x hx using hfs_meas x hx
  · filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with x hx using h_bound x hx
  · filter_upwards [h_cont] with a ha using ha x hx

theorem continuous_setToFun_of_dominated (hT : DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ T C) {fs : X → α → E}
    {bound : α → ℝ} (hfs_meas : ∀ x, AEStronglyMeasurable (fs x) μ)
    (h_bound : ∀ x, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖fs x a‖ ≤ bound a) (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ)
    (h_cont : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Continuous fun x => fs x a) : Continuous fun x => setToFun μ T hT (fs x) :=
  continuous_iff_continuousAt.mpr fun _ =>
    continuousAt_setToFun_of_dominated hT (Eventually.of_forall hfs_meas)
        (Eventually.of_forall h_bound) ‹_› <|
      h_cont.mono fun _ => Continuous.continuousAt

end Function

/-!
# Dynamical visibility of positive Cayley defects

A positive summable mass carried at nonzero points of the open unit disc has an inverse-radial
moment tower.  Every atom is amplified geometrically, without phase cancellation.  Consequently a
nonempty defect supports a positive exponential lower bound at every observation order, and a
bounded full tower forces the defect to be empty.

This is an index-free law.  The Riemann-Xi application supplies the masses from its endpoint source
and the disc points from the Li Cayley coordinate.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {I : Type*}

/-- The `n`-th inverse-radial moment of a positively marked Cayley divisor. -/
def inverseRadialMoment (a : I → ℝ) (w : I → ℂ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' i : I, a i * ‖w i‖⁻¹ ^ n

/-- Every summable inverse-radial moment is nonnegative when all marks are nonnegative. -/
theorem inverseRadialMoment_nonneg
    (a : I → ℝ) (w : I → ℂ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 ≤ a i) (n : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ inverseRadialMoment a w n := by
  rw [inverseRadialMoment]
  exact tsum_nonneg fun i => mul_nonneg (ha i) (pow_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (norm_nonneg _)) _)

/-- Every atom is a pointwise lower bound for the complete positive moment. -/
theorem le_inverseRadialMoment
    (a : I → ℝ) (w : I → ℂ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 ≤ a i)
    (hsum : ∀ n, Summable (fun i => a i * ‖w i‖⁻¹ ^ n))
    (i : I) (n : ℕ) :
    a i * ‖w i‖⁻¹ ^ n ≤ inverseRadialMoment a w n := by
  rw [inverseRadialMoment]
  exact (hsum n).le_tsum i fun j _ =>
    mul_nonneg (ha j) (pow_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (norm_nonneg _)) _)

/-- The zeroth inverse-radial moment is exactly the total marked mass. -/
theorem inverseRadialMoment_zero
    (a : I → ℝ) (w : I → ℂ) :
    inverseRadialMoment a w 0 = ∑' i, a i := by
  simp only [inverseRadialMoment, pow_zero, mul_one]

/-- **Positive Cayley-defect dynamical visibility.**  Every positive atom strictly inside the
unit disc supplies a positive exponential lower bound at every observation order. -/
theorem exists_exponential_lowerBound_inverseRadialMoment
    (a : I → ℝ) (w : I → ℂ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i)
    (hw0 : ∀ i, w i ≠ 0)
    (hw1 : ∀ i, ‖w i‖ < 1)
    (hsum : ∀ n, Summable (fun i => a i * ‖w i‖⁻¹ ^ n))
    (i : I) :
    ∃ m c : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ 1 < c ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, m * c ^ n ≤ inverseRadialMoment a w n := by
  refine ⟨a i, ‖w i‖⁻¹, ha i, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact (one_lt_inv₀ (norm_pos_iff.mpr (hw0 i))).mpr (hw1 i)
  · intro n
    exact le_inverseRadialMoment a w (fun j => (ha j).le) hsum i n

/-- A bounded inverse-radial tower has no positive atom in the open unit disc. -/
theorem isEmpty_of_bounded_inverseRadialMoment
    (a : I → ℝ) (w : I → ℂ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i)
    (hw0 : ∀ i, w i ≠ 0)
    (hw1 : ∀ i, ‖w i‖ < 1)
    (hsum : ∀ n, Summable (fun i => a i * ‖w i‖⁻¹ ^ n))
    (hbounded : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, inverseRadialMoment a w n ≤ K) :
    IsEmpty I := by
  constructor
  intro i
  obtain ⟨m, c, hm, hc, hlower⟩ :=
    exists_exponential_lowerBound_inverseRadialMoment a w ha hw0 hw1 hsum i
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := hbounded
  exact not_forall_mul_pow_le hc hm (fun n => (hlower n).trans (hK n))

end

end HTGeometry

/-!
# Mode-gauge holonomy of a thermal-horizon Bogoliubov kernel

A complex Bogoliubov kernel depends on independent conventions for incoming and outgoing mode
phases.  The alternating phase around a frequency rectangle cancels every output-only and
input-only phase.  Exponentiating gives the corresponding multiplicative kernel holonomy.

For the ideal thermal-horizon carrier, use outgoing frequency `x` and logarithmic incoming
frequency `ℓ`.  Its coupled phase is

`-i * inverseSurfaceGravity * x * ℓ`.

The rectangular defect is exactly

`-i * inverseSurfaceGravity * (x₁-x₂) * (ℓ₁-ℓ₂)`.

Consequently any frequency-row factor, including a Gamma phase depending only on outgoing
frequency, cancels from this fully separable-gauge-invariant observable.  This is an algebraic
statement about the stated kernel.  It does not assert that arbitrary frequency-dependent mode
rephasings are the physically preferred calibration, nor that exact exponential peeling holds for
every horizon.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Additive alternating defect around an input-output rectangle. -/
def rectanglePhaseDefect
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) : ℂ :=
  phase x₁ y₁ + phase x₂ y₂ - phase x₁ y₂ - phase x₂ y₁

/-- Independent row and column phase conventions cancel from the rectangular defect. -/
theorem rectanglePhaseDefect_separableGauge
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (row : X → ℂ) (column : Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) :
    rectanglePhaseDefect
        (fun x y => row x + phase x y + column y) x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ =
      rectanglePhaseDefect phase x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ := by
  simp only [rectanglePhaseDefect]
  ring

/-- Coupled phase of the ideal exponential-peeling horizon kernel in outgoing frequency and
logarithmic incoming frequency. -/
def thermalHorizonPhaseExponent
    (inverseSurfaceGravity outgoingFrequency logIncomingFrequency : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  -Complex.I * inverseSurfaceGravity * outgoingFrequency * logIncomingFrequency

/-- The unwrapped rectangular phase defect recovers the inverse-surface-gravity coefficient. -/
theorem rectanglePhaseDefect_thermalHorizonPhaseExponent
    (inverseSurfaceGravity x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℂ) :
    rectanglePhaseDefect
        (thermalHorizonPhaseExponent inverseSurfaceGravity) x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ =
      -Complex.I * inverseSurfaceGravity * (x₁ - x₂) * (ℓ₁ - ℓ₂) := by
  simp only [rectanglePhaseDefect, thermalHorizonPhaseExponent]
  ring

/-- Multiplicative alternating holonomy around an input-output rectangle. -/
def rectangleKernelHolonomy
    {X Y : Type*} (kernel : X → Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) : ℂ :=
  kernel x₁ y₁ * kernel x₂ y₂ /
    (kernel x₁ y₂ * kernel x₂ y₁)

/-- Exponential kernel generated by an additive phase. -/
def exponentialKernel
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ) : X → Y → ℂ :=
  fun x y => Complex.exp (phase x y)

/-- Rectangle holonomy of an exponential kernel is the exponential of its phase defect. -/
theorem rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) :
    rectangleKernelHolonomy (exponentialKernel phase) x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ =
      Complex.exp (rectanglePhaseDefect phase x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂) := by
  simp only [rectangleKernelHolonomy, exponentialKernel, rectanglePhaseDefect]
  rw [← Complex.exp_add, ← Complex.exp_add, ← Complex.exp_sub]
  congr 1
  ring

/-- Multiplicative rectangle holonomy is invariant under arbitrary separable exponential mode
calibrations. -/
theorem rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponential_separableGauge
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (row : X → ℂ) (column : Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) :
    rectangleKernelHolonomy
        (exponentialKernel (fun x y => row x + phase x y + column y))
        x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ =
      rectangleKernelHolonomy (exponentialKernel phase) x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ := by
  rw [rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel,
    rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel,
    rectanglePhaseDefect_separableGauge]

/-- Exact thermal-horizon rectangle holonomy.  Unlike the one-frequency Gamma phase, this
separable-gauge quotient contains only the coupled surface-gravity phase. -/
theorem rectangleKernelHolonomy_thermalHorizon
    (inverseSurfaceGravity x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℂ) :
    rectangleKernelHolonomy
        (exponentialKernel
          (thermalHorizonPhaseExponent inverseSurfaceGravity))
        x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ =
      Complex.exp
        (-Complex.I * inverseSurfaceGravity *
          (x₁ - x₂) * (ℓ₁ - ℓ₂)) := by
  rw [rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel,
    rectanglePhaseDefect_thermalHorizonPhaseExponent]

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.UnitaryPairTwistHardyBound
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.UnimodularMulLp

open Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

universe u

/-- A quantitatively bounded family of invertible operators between two particle-number-indexed
Hardy subspaces. The ambient spaces already encode the analytic Hardy-domain regularity. -/
structure HardyIntertwinerFamily
    (E : ℕ → Type u) [∀ n, NormedAddCommGroup (E n)] [∀ n, NormedSpace ℂ (E n)]
    (source target : ∀ n, Submodule ℂ (E n)) where
  gamma : ℝ
  gammaInv : ℝ
  one_le_gamma : 1 ≤ gamma
  one_le_gammaInv : 1 ≤ gammaInv
  forward : ∀ n, E n →L[ℂ] E n
  inverse : ∀ n, E n →L[ℂ] E n
  forward_inverse : ∀ n, forward n * inverse n = 1
  inverse_forward : ∀ n, inverse n * forward n = 1
  maps_forward : ∀ n, MapsTo (forward n) (source n) (target n)
  maps_inverse : ∀ n, MapsTo (inverse n) (target n) (source n)
  norm_forward : ∀ n, ‖forward n‖ ≤ gamma ^ n
  norm_inverse : ∀ n, ‖inverse n‖ ≤ gammaInv ^ n

namespace HardyIntertwinerFamily

variable {E : ℕ → Type u} [∀ n, NormedAddCommGroup (E n)] [∀ n, NormedSpace ℂ (E n)]
  {source middle target : ∀ n, Submodule ℂ (E n)}

/-- Reverse a bounded Hardy intertwiner family, exchanging its two quantitative constants. -/
def symm (J : HardyIntertwinerFamily E source target) :
    HardyIntertwinerFamily E target source where
  gamma := J.gammaInv
  gammaInv := J.gamma
  one_le_gamma := J.one_le_gammaInv
  one_le_gammaInv := J.one_le_gamma
  forward := J.inverse
  inverse := J.forward
  forward_inverse := J.inverse_forward
  inverse_forward := J.forward_inverse
  maps_forward := J.maps_inverse
  maps_inverse := J.maps_forward
  norm_forward := J.norm_inverse
  norm_inverse := J.norm_forward

/-- Composition of Hardy intertwiner families. Exponential bases multiply in the exact order
forced by the forward and inverse compositions. -/
def comp (I : HardyIntertwinerFamily E middle target)
    (J : HardyIntertwinerFamily E source middle) :
    HardyIntertwinerFamily E source target where
  gamma := I.gamma * J.gamma
  gammaInv := J.gammaInv * I.gammaInv
  one_le_gamma := one_le_mul_of_one_le_of_one_le I.one_le_gamma J.one_le_gamma
  one_le_gammaInv := one_le_mul_of_one_le_of_one_le J.one_le_gammaInv I.one_le_gammaInv
  forward := fun n => I.forward n * J.forward n
  inverse := fun n => J.inverse n * I.inverse n
  forward_inverse := by
    intro n
    calc
      (I.forward n * J.forward n) * (J.inverse n * I.inverse n) =
          I.forward n * (J.forward n * J.inverse n) * I.inverse n := by
            noncomm_ring
      _ = I.forward n * 1 * I.inverse n := by rw [J.forward_inverse n]
      _ = 1 := by simpa using I.forward_inverse n
  inverse_forward := by
    intro n
    calc
      (J.inverse n * I.inverse n) * (I.forward n * J.forward n) =
          J.inverse n * (I.inverse n * I.forward n) * J.forward n := by
            noncomm_ring
      _ = J.inverse n * 1 * J.forward n := by rw [I.inverse_forward n]
      _ = 1 := by simpa using J.inverse_forward n
  maps_forward := by
    intro n x hx
    exact I.maps_forward n (J.maps_forward n hx)
  maps_inverse := by
    intro n x hx
    exact J.maps_inverse n (I.maps_inverse n hx)
  norm_forward := by
    intro n
    calc
      ‖I.forward n * J.forward n‖ ≤ ‖I.forward n‖ * ‖J.forward n‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
      _ ≤ I.gamma ^ n * J.gamma ^ n := mul_le_mul (I.norm_forward n) (J.norm_forward n)
          (norm_nonneg _) (pow_nonneg (le_trans zero_le_one I.one_le_gamma) _)
      _ = (I.gamma * J.gamma) ^ n := (mul_pow _ _ _).symm
  norm_inverse := by
    intro n
    calc
      ‖J.inverse n * I.inverse n‖ ≤ ‖J.inverse n‖ * ‖I.inverse n‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
      _ ≤ J.gammaInv ^ n * I.gammaInv ^ n :=
        mul_le_mul (J.norm_inverse n) (I.norm_inverse n) (norm_nonneg _)
          (pow_nonneg (le_trans zero_le_one J.one_le_gammaInv) _)
      _ = (J.gammaInv * I.gammaInv) ^ n := (mul_pow _ _ _).symm

end HardyIntertwinerFamily

/-- Existence of one all-particle Hardy intertwiner with uniform exponential constants. -/
def HasHardyIntertwiner
    (E : ℕ → Type u) [∀ n, NormedAddCommGroup (E n)] [∀ n, NormedSpace ℂ (E n)]
    (source target : ∀ n, Submodule ℂ (E n)) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (HardyIntertwinerFamily E source target)

/-- A bounded scalar CDD intertwiner transports the all-particle Hardy intertwiner property in
both directions. -/
theorem hasHardyIntertwiner_iff_of_scalarCDD
    {E : ℕ → Type u} [∀ n, NormedAddCommGroup (E n)] [∀ n, NormedSpace ℂ (E n)]
    {dressed base reference : ∀ n, Submodule ℂ (E n)}
    (J : HardyIntertwinerFamily E dressed base) :
    HasHardyIntertwiner E base reference ↔ HasHardyIntertwiner E dressed reference := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨I⟩
    exact ⟨I.comp J⟩
  · rintro ⟨I⟩
    exact ⟨I.comp J.symm⟩

section Exchange

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℂ V]

/-- Central scalar dressing of a matrix-valued two-body exchange factor. -/

/-!
# Finite Boltzmann relations

For a nonempty finite state space, microcanonical entropy is the logarithm of
the zero-inverse-temperature partition function.  This identifies the uniform
Gibbs population, Wightman kernel, replica purity, energy moments, and
independent-system tensor product with exact exponential entropy factors.

At zero inverse temperature every Gibbs population affinity and every induced
walk affinity vanishes.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- The microcanonical entropy is the logarithm of the canonical partition at zero inverse
temperature. -/
theorem finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_log_finiteGibbsPartition_zero
    (I : Type*) [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I =
      Real.log (HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition 0 energy) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero]
  rfl

/-- The zero-inverse-temperature partition is the exponential of microcanonical entropy. -/
theorem finiteGibbsPartition_zero_eq_exp_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    (I : Type*) [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition 0 energy =
      Real.exp (finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero, finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy,
    Real.exp_log]
  positivity

/-- At zero inverse temperature every Gibbs population is the uniform microcanonical weight. -/
theorem finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight 0 energy i = microcanonicalWeight I i := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight, HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero]
  simp [microcanonicalWeight]

/-- Each zero-inverse-temperature Gibbs population is the inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight 0 energy i =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  letI : Nonempty I := ⟨i⟩
  rw [finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight]
  simpa [microcanonicalWeight] using
    (exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_card_inv I).symm

/-- The zero-inverse-temperature Wightman kernel is the uniform microcanonical weight. -/
theorem finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i j : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i j = microcanonicalWeight I i := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight, HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero]
  simp [microcanonicalWeight]

/-- Every zero-inverse-temperature Wightman kernel entry is the inverse Boltzmann
multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i j : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i j =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  letI : Nonempty I := ⟨i⟩
  rw [finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight]
  simpa [microcanonicalWeight] using
    (exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_card_inv I).symm

/-- Zero-temperature Gibbs purity is the inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteGibbsPurity_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPurity 0 energy =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPurity_zero,
    exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_card_inv]
  simp [one_div]

/-- The diagonal squared mass of the zero-inverse-temperature thermofield kernel is the inverse
Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem sum_sq_diag_finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_entropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    ∑ i, HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i i ^ 2 =

/-- The off-diagonal squared thermofield mass at zero inverse temperature is one minus the
inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem sum_offDiagonal_sq_finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_one_sub_exp_neg_entropy

/-!
# Euler normal shifts are Gamma-shape chiral shifts

For an exponential ray of rate `r`, put

`λ = i r / (2π)`,
`E_r(s) = 1 - exp(-rs)`, and
`q_r(s) = rs exp(rs/2) / (4π²)`.

Euler reflection gives the exact endpoint weld

`q_r(s) E_r(s) Γ(λs) Γ(-λs) = 1`.

The finite plaquette law for symmetric/chiral carriers then identifies a spectral normal shift of
the Euler factor with the corresponding Gamma shape shift.  For `r = log p`, this is the local
factor of `ζ(s-α)/ζ(s+α)`.  No zeta zero, analytic continuation, or RH assumption occurs.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

open Complex GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- Imaginary Gamma slope attached to an exponential rate. -/
def exponentialRayGammaSlope (rate : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  Complex.I * rate / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))

/-- Inverse local Euler factor on one exponential ray. -/
def exponentialRayEulerFactor (rate s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  1 - Complex.exp (-rate * s)

/-- Explicit DA gauge relating the reciprocal symmetric Gamma endpoint to the Euler factor. -/
def exponentialRayGammaGauge (rate s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  rate * s * Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) / (4 * (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2)

/-- At rate `log p`, the exponential-ray factor is literally the corpus's entire inverse local
Euler factor. -/
theorem exponentialRayEulerFactor_logPrime_eq_eulerInvFactor (p : ℕ) (s : ℂ) :
    exponentialRayEulerFactor (Real.log p : ℂ) s = eulerInvFactor p s := by
  unfold exponentialRayEulerFactor eulerInvFactor
  congr 2
  ring

private theorem gamma_symmetric_endpoint_mul (u : ℂ)
    (hu : u ≠ 0) (hsin : Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * u) ≠ 0) :
    u * Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * u) *
        (Complex.Gamma u * Complex.Gamma (-u)) = -(Real.pi : ℂ) := by
  have hrec :
      Complex.Gamma (1 - u) = (-u) * Complex.Gamma (-u) := by
    convert Complex.Gamma_add_one (-u) (neg_ne_zero.mpr hu) using 1 ; ring
  have href := Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_one_sub u
  rw [hrec] at href
  have href' :
      (Complex.Gamma u * ((-u) * Complex.Gamma (-u))) *
          Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * u) = (Real.pi : ℂ) :=
    (eq_div_iff hsin).mp href
  calc
    u * Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * u) *
        (Complex.Gamma u * Complex.Gamma (-u)) =
        -((Complex.Gamma u * ((-u) * Complex.Gamma (-u))) *
          Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * u)) := by ring
    _ = -(Real.pi : ℂ) := by rw [href']

private theorem sin_exponentialRayGammaSlope (rate s : ℂ) :
    Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * exponentialRayGammaSlope rate * s) =
      Complex.I / 2 *
        (Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) - Complex.exp (-(rate * s / 2))) := by
  have hpi : (Real.pi : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr Real.pi_ne_zero
  rw [show (Real.pi : ℂ) * exponentialRayGammaSlope rate * s =
      (rate * s / 2) * Complex.I by
    unfold exponentialRayGammaSlope
    field_simp [hpi]]
  rw [Complex.sin_mul_I]
  unfold Complex.sinh
  ring

private theorem gauge_mul_euler_eq_neg_slope_sin_div_pi
    (rate s : ℂ) :
    exponentialRayGammaGauge rate s * exponentialRayEulerFactor rate s =
      -(exponentialRayGammaSlope rate * s *
        Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * exponentialRayGammaSlope rate * s)) /
          (Real.pi : ℂ) := by
  have hpi : (Real.pi : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr Real.pi_ne_zero
  have hexp :
      Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) * Complex.exp (-rate * s) =
        Complex.exp (-(rate * s / 2)) := by
    rw [← Complex.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  rw [sin_exponentialRayGammaSlope]
  unfold exponentialRayGammaGauge exponentialRayEulerFactor exponentialRayGammaSlope
  calc
    rate * s * Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) / (4 * (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2) *
        (1 - Complex.exp (-rate * s)) =
      rate * s / (4 * (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2) *
        (Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) -
          Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) * Complex.exp (-rate * s)) := by ring
    _ = rate * s / (4 * (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2) *
        (Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) -
          Complex.exp (-(rate * s / 2))) := by rw [hexp]
    _ = -(Complex.I * rate / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ)) * s *
          (Complex.I / 2 *
            (Complex.exp (rate * s / 2) -
              Complex.exp (-(rate * s / 2))))) /
        (Real.pi : ℂ) := by
      field_simp [hpi]
      rw [Complex.I_sq]
      ring

/-- **Local Euler--Gamma endpoint weld.**  The reciprocal symmetric Gamma endpoint is exactly an
inverse Euler factor times an explicit rational/exponential gauge. -/
theorem exponentialRayGammaGauge_mul_eulerFactor_mul_symmetricEndpoint
    (rate s : ℂ)
    (hu : exponentialRayGammaSlope rate * s ≠ 0)
    (hsin : Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) *
      (exponentialRayGammaSlope rate * s)) ≠ 0) :
    exponentialRayGammaGauge rate s * exponentialRayEulerFactor rate s *
        symmetricShapeCarrier Complex.Gamma
          (exponentialRayGammaSlope rate) 0 s = 1 := by
  have hpi : (Real.pi : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr Real.pi_ne_zero
  rw [gauge_mul_euler_eq_neg_slope_sin_div_pi]
